name: 3Brain
description: Developing high-resolution microelectrode array (MEA) platforms that capture brain cell electrophysiology in vitro for neuroscience research and drug discovery.
analyst_note: 3Brain sits in the ex vivo electrophysiology tools segment, differentiated by its bidirectional CMOS-MEA arrays at 4,096-electrode density, a specification tier above most competing platforms in the organoid and brain-slice research market. With no disclosed clinical or in vivo pathway, its microchip-based technology is best understood as research infrastructure rather than translational technology.

name: ABILITY Neurotech
description: Developing implantable neural interface (BCI) to restore autonomy in paralysis by capturing, transmitting, analyzing, and stimulating brain activity.
analyst_note: ABILITY Neurotech is differentiated by its fully implantable, battery-free ECoG architecture with 50 Mbps lossless data transmission, a throughput substantially above current competitors in the implantable BCI space. As a 2025 Wyss Center spin-off entering first clinical trials in the Netherlands and Austria, it sits at the earliest stage of clinical translation in a field dominated by longer-established players like Blackrock Neurotech and Synchron.

name: Affectable Sleep
description: Developing an EEG sleep headband using precisely timed auditory neurostimulation to enhance slow-wave sleep and restorative sleep function.
analyst_note: Affectable Sleep sits in closed-loop sleep neurotechnology, combining EEG monitoring with timed auditory stimulation in a consumer headband. Its current stage appears pre-commercial, with grant-supported user testing and early manufacturing work.

name: Aleph Neuro
description: Building non-invasive, ultrasound-based brain imaging technology intended to serve as a hardware foundation for future brain-computer interfaces.
analyst_note: Non-invasive ultrasound imaging at MRI-like resolution would remove one of the two hardware bottlenecks that have kept BCI confined to invasive implants or blurry scalp sensing. The claims are unverified outside the company's own announcement, and the "telepathic future" framing runs well ahead of any demonstrated decoding capability.

name: Aleva Neurotherapeutics
description: Implantable MEMS‑based directional deep brain stimulation (DBS) system improving precision and outcomes in Parkinson’s and essential tremor.
analyst_note: Aleva Neurotherapeutics is positioned in the DBS hardware segment with a MEMS-based directional lead design that offers finer current steering than conventional cylindrical electrodes, targeting improved side-effect profiles in Parkinson's and essential tremor. With CE marking and Series C+ funding, it sits further along the commercialization curve than most neuromodulation startups but faces entrenched competition from Medtronic, Abbott, and Boston Scientific.

name: Alljoined
description: Building foundation models for brain data that decode visual perception from non-invasive EEG signals, reconstructing seen images from neural recordings.
analyst_note: Alljoined is best understood as a research-infrastructure company building open-source EEG-to-image foundation models, sitting in the same data-platform layer as Karavela AI and Nubrain but differentiated by its focus on visual decoding and multi-subject generalization. Its open-release strategy prioritizes ecosystem building over proprietary moat, making its near-term monetization path less clear than product-oriented BCI companies.

name: Alto Neuroscience
description: Developing precision psychiatric medicines by leveraging neurobiology to predict and improve treatment response.
analyst_note: Alto Neuroscience is best understood as a precision psychiatry drug company rather than a neurotech device company, using EEG-derived neural phenotyping to match patients to proprietary compounds across depression, PTSD, and schizophrenia. Its 2024 IPO and four active Phase 2 trials position it as one of the few publicly traded companies attempting to close the loop between brain biomarkers and psychiatric drug selection.

name: Altoida
description: Providing a digital multimodal NeuroMarker platform to objectively assess and monitor cognitive function and detect early signs of neurodegenerative decline.
analyst_note: Altoida is differentiated by its AR-based multimodal cognitive assessment capturing 600+ biomarkers in a 10-minute session, giving it a broader signal surface than most digital cognitive screening tools. The platform sits in the investigational segment for MCI and Alzheimer's detection, with validation across 42,000+ tests but no regulatory clearance for diagnostic use.

name: Amber Therapeutics
description: Developing an adaptive, implantable neuromodulation device for women’s mixed urinary incontinence.
analyst_note: Amber Therapeutics occupies a distinctive niche as the only implantable neuromodulation company specifically targeting mixed urinary incontinence via pudendal nerve stimulation, a condition underserved by existing sacral neuromodulation devices. Its landmark $100M Series A in 2024 signals significant investor conviction, though the company remains pre-approval and faces the clinical and regulatory burden typical of novel implantable indications.

name: Ampa Health
description: Developing a portable transcranial magnetic stimulation system to expand access to clinically validated neuromodulation treatments for mental health disorders.
analyst_note: Ampa Health is positioned around expanding TMS access by miniaturizing the delivery system into a portable form factor, addressing the key bottleneck of clinic-bound infrastructure that limits current TMS adoption. With FDA clearance and seed-stage funding, it sits at an early commercial stage in a TMS market otherwise dominated by large-footprint systems from BrainsWay and Magstim.

name: Anthriq
description: Developing non-invasive EEG-based BCI headsets and a full-stack biosignal ecosystem, hardware, SDK, APIs, for real-time brain-tech interaction.
analyst_note: Anthriq is best understood as a developer-infrastructure play in the biosignal space, packaging wireless EEG hardware with a full-stack SDK and API layer aimed at enabling third-party applications rather than serving end users directly. This positions it adjacent to Arctop and BrainBit in the BCI middleware segment, though with a stronger hardware-plus-software bundle rather than a purely software-agnostic approach.

name: ANUEVO
description: Providing a non-invasive transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation system to restore motor function in people with chronic spinal cord injury.
analyst_note: Aneuvo's FDA clearance and prior CE mark for ExaStim make it one of the few transcutaneous SCS companies with both regulatory approval and home-use indication rather than clinic-only trial data. Its patent dispute with Onward Medical, resolved in Aneuvo's favor at the Unified Patent Court, signals a competitive and increasingly commercial transcutaneous stimulation market rather than a purely early-research field.

name: Aora
description: Developing a behind-the-ear neurofeedback wearable for cognitive load, neural recovery, burnout risk, and real-time brain-state tracking.
analyst_note: Aora appears positioned as an early consumer brain-health wearable around lightweight, continuous mental-state tracking. Its current public materials emphasize pre-order and field-test activity, with limited independent validation or regulatory detail available.

name: Apollo Neuro
description: A wearable “touch therapy” device using calming vibrations to enhance stress resilience, focus, and sleep via SmartVibes AI.
analyst_note: Apollo Neuro sits in the consumer wellness segment as a vibrotactile wearable positioned around vagus nerve activation for stress, sleep, and focus, backed by an unusually extensive clinical evidence base for a non-medical device. Its direct-to-consumer distribution and Series A funding differentiate it from clinical neuromodulation companies, though the wellness-grade regulatory pathway limits its clinical credibility ceiling.

name: Arctop
description: Developing a hardware-agnostic brain-computer interface platform that decodes neural activity to deliver real-time cognitive and intention metrics via developer APIs and SDKs.
analyst_note: Arctop is differentiated by its hardware-agnostic positioning, offering a developer-facing SDK that abstracts brain signal decoding across any EEG hardware rather than selling proprietary sensors. This infrastructure-layer approach targets a different buyer than most BCI companies, appealing to gaming, education, and enterprise developers seeking to integrate neural metrics without building neuroscience expertise in-house.

name: Artiria Medical
description: Developing micro-articulated guidewire systems with dynamic tip manipulation for minimally invasive neurovascular stroke interventions.
analyst_note: Artiria Medical stands out in the neurovascular tools segment as one of very few startups focused specifically on guidewire navigation rather than thrombectomy devices, giving it a narrower competitive set but a clear procedural pain point. With FDA clearance, 50+ clinical cases, and Series A funding, it sits further along the commercialization curve than most neurotech startups at comparable scale.

name: Atlas
description: Developing a behind-the-ear EEG wearable that quantifies cognitive signals such as readiness and focus for real-world monitoring and performance contexts.
analyst_note: Atlas is positioned as a consumer EEG wearable emphasizing a discrete behind-the-ear form factor that avoids the headband aesthetic typical of competitors like Muse and BrainBit. The grant-funded, wellness-focused product targets behavioral feedback loops linking cognitive state to daily activity, though it remains pre-commercial with no disclosed regulatory or clinical pathway.

name: Attune Neurosciences
description: Developing wearable low-intensity focused ultrasound neuromodulation systems for deep-brain targets across chronic pain, depression, and related indications.
analyst_note: Attune Neurosciences sits in the focused ultrasound neuromodulation segment, with a wearable headband format aimed at making deep-brain stimulation more deployable outside hospital-based systems. Its current positioning is clinical-stage and research-backed, with ARPA-H supported work in chronic pain and depression biomarkers.

name: Audicin
description: Providing audio-based nervous system regulation using brainwave entrainment and wearable biometric data across app, headband, and SDK formats.
analyst_note: The product runs as a regulation layer inside existing wearable ecosystems, monetizing through an SDK instead of proprietary hardware, which is a distribution bet as much as a neurotech one. No direct neural measurement sits behind the brainwave-entrainment claims just yet, keeping it at the wellness end of the category despite the neurotech framing.

name: Aural Analytics
description: Delivering clinical-grade, non-invasive speech analytics to assess neurological health and monitor neurodegenerative diseases.
analyst_note: Aural Analytics is best understood as an acquired speech-biomarker capability now embedded within Linus Health's broader multimodal cognitive assessment platform, rather than an independent company. Its differentiation lay in non-invasive vocal analysis for neurological disease detection, a modality that gains more clinical weight when combined with Linus Health's existing digital cognitive tools.

name: Aurenar
description: Developing a non-invasive, single-use transauricular vagus nerve stimulation device to reduce inflammation-driven complications in ICU stroke patients.
analyst_note: Transauricular vagus nerve stimulation gives Aurenar a low-friction entry point into acute ICU care, targeting inflammation-driven secondary brain injury rather than building a broad neuromodulation platform from day one. FDA Breakthrough Device status and pilot data from Washington University carry it further along the translation path than most seed-stage neuromodulation companies typically reach this early.

name: AWEAR
description: Developing an ear-worn EEG wearable that tracks brainwave patterns and provides AI-guided stress and emotional-wellness insights.
analyst_note: AWEAR sits in the consumer mental-wellness wearable segment, using ear-worn EEG as the sensing layer for stress and emotional-state feedback. Its positioning is differentiated by the attempt to make continuous brain monitoring fit into the behavioral loop established by mainstream health wearables.

name: Axoft
description: Creating ultrasoft, brain‑mimicking implantable interfaces that reduce tissue damage, maintain high electrode density, and enable stable long‑term single‑neuron communication.
analyst_note: Axoft is differentiated by its ultrasoft Fleuron material, which is orders of magnitude more compliant than standard polyimide probes, addressing the chronic tissue-scarring problem that limits long-term signal stability in conventional intracortical implants. With first-in-human cases completed in 2025, it has advanced further into clinical translation than most materials-science-focused BCI startups at seed stage.

name: Axorus
description: Developing a retinal prosthesis in the form of a photoacoustic contact lens and laser glasses system to non-invasively restore vision in degenerative blindness.
analyst_note: Axorus occupies a narrow and technically distinctive position in the visual prosthesis space, using photoacoustic stimulation delivered via a contact-lens-and-glasses system rather than surgically implanted retinal electrodes. This non-invasive approach to retinal stimulation is differentiated from both implantable competitors like Second Sight and cortical visual prostheses, though it remains at the preclinical stage with published proof-of-concept only.

name: Beacon Biosignals
description: Accelerating precision neuroscience in clinical trials by capturing and analyzing sleep EEG with AI-powered biomarkers.
analyst_note: Beacon Biosignals is positioned as the leading pharma-facing EEG analytics platform, using a foundation model trained on millions of hours of sleep EEG data to extract CNS drug biomarkers for clinical trial endpoints. Its $86M Series B, FDA-cleared Waveband device, and partnerships with Takeda and UCB place it among the most commercially advanced neurotech startups in the biopharma services segment.

name: Biological Input Output Systems
description: Developing an implantable universal neural interface that enables intuitive two-way communication between the nervous system and external devices to restore movement and sensation.
analyst_note: Biological Input Output Systems is differentiated by targeting the peripheral nervous system rather than the brain for its universal neural interface, avoiding craniotomy while enabling bidirectional prosthetic control through adaptive decoding algorithms. The company remains at an early and opaque stage with limited public disclosure on funding or regulatory progress, making its commercial trajectory difficult to assess.

name: Bioness Medical
description: Providing functional electrical stimulation and neuromodulation devices for rehabilitation after stroke, spinal cord injury, and other neurological conditions.
analyst_note: Bioness Medical is best understood as a mature rehabilitation-device incumbent rather than an emerging startup, now operating as a private-equity-backed consolidation platform under Accelmed Partners following its 2026 divestiture from Bioventus. Its recent acquisitions of PoNS and Harmonic Bionics position it as an active roll-up aggregator within neuro-rehabilitation rather than a single-product innovator.

name: BIOS Health
description: Advancing precision medicine by interpreting the nervous system’s real-time data using AI-driven neural interfaces.
analyst_note: BIOS Health is best understood as a neural-data analytics platform targeting pharma rather than patients, using AI to decode real-time neural signals and correlate them with drug and device efficacy at millisecond resolution. This positions it as infrastructure for precision bioelectronic medicine trials rather than a therapeutic product company, with Series A funding and partnerships across chronic disease indications.

name: BioSerenity
description: Providing connected EEG, sleep, and cardiology monitoring devices paired with an in-house AI foundation model for clinical signal interpretation.
analyst_note: A decade of hospital deployments and an FDA-cleared EEG device give BioSerenity a data and distribution base that few AI-diagnostics entrants can match, now being redirected into its own foundation model, BioSerenity-E1. Routine pre-screening of standard EEGs since December 2025 marks an early, concrete deployment of that model rather than a research demo, a distinction that separates it from earlier-stage EEG foundation model plays.

name: Bitbrain
description: Empowering multimodal brain–body research with wearable EEG and biosensor systems, backed by AI-powered data platforms.
analyst_note: Bitbrain is positioned as a multimodal research-hardware company offering synchronized EEG, biosignal, and eye-tracking systems designed for complex experimental workflows requiring 35+ simultaneous sensor channels. Its differentiation lies in hardware modularity and the breadth of simultaneous physiological signals rather than clinical application, placing it firmly in the research-tools market adjacent to g.tec and Brain Products.

name: Blackrock Neurotech
description: Developer of the Utah Array, the first FDA-cleared BCI implant, enabling long-term neural recording and brain-controlled devices.
analyst_note: Blackrock Neurotech is the longest-established intracortical BCI company, with the Utah Array having accumulated more documented long-term human implant data than any competing device in the field. Its Series B funding and FDA Breakthrough Designation position it as the reference platform against which newer implantable BCI entrants are benchmarked, though it faces increasing competitive pressure from companies pursuing less invasive approaches.

name: Bottneuro
description: Developing a personalized, non-invasive transcranial electrical stimulation system for home-based treatment support in cognitive and neurological disorders.
analyst_note: Bottneuro is differentiated by its MRI-individualized, 3D-printed electrode montage approach to home-based tES, offering a level of stimulation personalization that generic consumer tDCS devices do not attempt. As a University of Basel spin-off with Swiss and UK device registration, it sits in a narrow segment between clinical-grade neuromodulation and consumer brain stimulation products.

name: BRAIN.Q
description: Developing non-invasive, AI-driven neuromodulation systems to promote neuroplasticity and functional recovery after neurological injury.
analyst_note: BRAIN.Q is differentiated by its AI-personalized electromagnetic field therapy approach to post-stroke recovery, where stimulation parameters are tailored to individual neural network patterns rather than delivered at fixed protocols. With CE marking, Phase 2 data showing a threefold improvement in functional independence, and Series B funding, it sits among the more clinically advanced non-invasive stroke-recovery platforms.

name: BrainBit
description: Delivering wearable, dry-electrode EEG headbands and SDKs for real-time brain-state monitoring in wellness, gaming, and neurofeedback.
analyst_note: BrainBit is positioned as a low-cost, developer-accessible EEG hardware platform, offering dry-electrode headbands with cross-platform SDK support across six operating systems and Unity. Its primary differentiation is the breadth of its developer toolchain rather than signal quality or clinical validation, placing it in the prototyping and consumer-research tier below medical-grade EEG systems.

name: BrainCapture
description: Expanding access to neurological diagnostics by deploying portable EEG systems and telemedicine tools for remote epilepsy detection.
analyst_note: BrainCapture is differentiated by its explicit focus on affordable, nurse-administered epilepsy EEG in resource-limited settings across Africa and South Asia, a deployment context most EEG companies do not target. With CE Class IIA MDR certification and a 27-channel portable amplifier, it occupies a global-health niche that is commercially smaller but competitively uncontested relative to the ambulatory EEG market in developed economies.

name: BrainCheck
description: Providing a software-based cognitive assessment platform for rapid screening, monitoring, and diagnosis support across neurological and mental health conditions.
analyst_note: BrainCheck is positioned as a software-only cognitive screening platform with FDA clearance, targeting rapid in-clinic assessment across dementia, concussion, and general cognitive decline without requiring specialized neuropsychological staff. Its differentiation lies in clinical workflow integration and regulatory status rather than novel biomarker technology, placing it in the digital cognitive assessment tier alongside Cogstate and Cambridge Cognition.

name: BrainCo
description: Developing non-invasive brain-computer interface wearables for cognitive training, education, and assistive control using EEG-based neural signal decoding.
analyst_note: BrainCo spans two distinct product lines ‚Äî a consumer EEG headband for cognitive training and an EMG-driven prosthetics division for upper-limb rehabilitation ‚Äî making it one of the few neurotech companies operating across both the consumer wellness and medical device segments simultaneously. This breadth creates a broader addressable market but diffuses its positioning relative to pure-play competitors in either vertical.

name: BrainKey
description: Visualizing users' MRI scans in 3D and delivers personalized brain health insights-including brain age and lifestyle recommendations.
analyst_note: BrainKey is positioned around a consumer-facing brain-age metric derived from AI analysis of standard MRI scans, a concept that straddles wellness and clinical neuroimaging without fully committing to either regulatory pathway. The seed-stage company sits in a segment adjacent to clinical AI neuroimaging tools like Brainomix and BrainQuant but is differentiated by its direct-to-consumer orientation and lifestyle-health framing.

name: Brainomix
description: Developing AI-driven neuroimaging software to support rapid, standardized analysis of brain scans for stroke and other neurological conditions.
analyst_note: Brainomix is one of the most commercially advanced AI neuroimaging companies in stroke, with eight FDA clearances, Series C+ funding, and a secondary lung-imaging platform developed in partnership with Boehringer Ingelheim. Its dual-platform strategy across stroke and pulmonary fibrosis is atypical for neurotech companies and diversifies its revenue base, though it also dilutes its positioning as a pure neurotechnology play.

name: BrainPatch
description: Developing a non-invasive neurostimulation headset that induces meditative states to support stress reduction and mental wellness.
analyst_note: BrainPatch sits in the consumer neurostimulation wellness segment with a multimodal headset combining vagus nerve stimulation, vestibular stimulation, and auditory activation for meditation and stress reduction. Its CE-marked, direct-to-consumer positioning places it among a growing cohort of wellness-grade brain-stimulation devices, though the combination of three stimulation modalities in one device is technically distinctive relative to single-modality competitors.

name: Brainphonics
description: Developing EEG-based objective hearing assessment software that maps brain responses to speech and everyday sounds.
analyst_note: Brainphonics is best understood as a clinical audiology tool built on neural speech tracking, a niche that sits apart from the broader EEG diagnostics space by targeting objective hearing assessment in non-cooperating populations. Its KU Leuven pedigree and clinical validation at UZ Leuven position it closer to translation than most grant-stage EEG startups, though commercialization remains early.

name: Brainquant
description: Developing AI-powered MRI software for early non-invasive detection and diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases.
analyst_note: BrainQuant appears positioned to fill a specific gap in the dementia diagnostics pipeline by offering a software-only ASL-MRI analysis layer that approximates PET-level perfusion data without radioactive tracers. As a freshly launched Wyss Center spin-off with no external funding round, it sits at the earliest stage of commercial translation in a competitive AI neuroimaging field.

name: BrainScan
description: Providing AI-assisted analysis of non-contrast brain CT scans to detect and prioritize intracranial pathologies for clinical workflows.
analyst_note: BrainScan is positioned as a broad-spectrum AI brain CT analyzer detecting 30 pathologies from non-contrast scans, a wider diagnostic scope than most competitors that focus on single conditions like stroke or hemorrhage. With CE Class IIa marking and a hardware-agnostic SaaS delivery model, it targets integration into existing radiology workflows across European and UK hospital systems.

name: BrainScope
description: Developing non-invasive EEG-based diagnostic devices to rapidly assess traumatic brain injury and support clinical decision-making at the point of care.
analyst_note: BrainScope holds the distinction of being one of the first FDA-approved AI/ML devices in neurology, with its EEG-based traumatic brain injury assessment demonstrating 99% sensitivity for intracranial hemorrhage detection and documented 50% reductions in unnecessary CT scans at major health systems. Its PMA-level regulatory status is a significant competitive moat in the point-of-care brain injury assessment segment.

name: BrainSightAI
description: Generating personalized, AI-based connectome maps from MRI (VoxelBox) to support surgical planning and psychiatric diagnostics.
analyst_note: BrainSightAI is differentiated by its AI-driven connectome mapping from standard MRI data, serving a primarily Indian hospital network of 40+ institutions for surgical planning and psychiatric diagnostics. Its regional positioning in an underserved neurosurgery market gives it a distinct deployment context from US- and Europe-focused neuroimaging AI companies, though it limits near-term addressable market scale.

name: BrainsWay
description: Developing non-invasive deep transcranial magnetic stimulation systems for the treatment of psychiatric and neurological disorders.
analyst_note: BrainsWay is the most broadly FDA-cleared deep TMS company, with distinct clearances across MDD, OCD, smoking cessation, and anxiety, plus a recent adolescent expansion, giving it the widest approved indication set of any TMS system on the market. As a publicly traded company with established clinical reimbursement pathways, it is best understood as an incumbent platform in non-invasive psychiatric neuromodulation rather than an emerging startup.

name: BrainTrip
description: Providing EEG-based brain mapping and neurofeedback software to support personalized assessment and training of brain function.
analyst_note: BrainTrip sits in the practitioner-facing neurofeedback software segment, translating quantitative EEG data into brain maps and personalized training protocols for clinicians, coaches, and performance practitioners. Its positioning is best understood as clinical workflow tooling for the existing neurofeedback practitioner base rather than a novel biomarker or therapeutic platform.

name: BRNLIT AI
description: Consumer app that uses a one-time personalized EEG measurement to generate AI-tailored light signals intended to improve focus and mental performance.
analyst_note: BRNLIT AI sits in the lightweight consumer neuro-personalization segment, using a one-time EEG measurement to generate tailored light signals for focus and performance. It is more of a personalized wellness app concept than a defensible neurotechnology platform at this stage.

name: Bía Neuroscience
description: Developing a smart sleep mask that uses fNIRS-based neurofeedback and audio cues to monitor and improve sleep quality.
analyst_note: Bía Neuroscience sits in the consumer sleep neurotechnology segment, where brain sensing is used to support wellness-oriented sleep feedback and personalization. Its positioning is differentiated by the use of fNIRS in a sleep-mask form factor, placing it closer to adaptive sleep wearables than conventional EEG-based sleep trackers.

name: Cadence Neuroscience
description: Developing an implantable neuromodulation therapy for drug-resistant focal epilepsy using personalized cortical stimulation and brain-activity monitoring.
analyst_note: Cadence Neuroscience sits in the implanted epilepsy neuromodulation segment, with chronic subthreshold cortical stimulation used to personalize therapy around patient-specific brain activity. Its positioning is differentiated by a reversible cortical stimulation approach for focal drug-resistant epilepsy, placing it alongside established implantable epilepsy therapies while using a distinct stimulation strategy.

name: Cahira Technologies
description: Developing autonomous, non-surgical nanoelectronic brain implants that self-deploy in target regions to treat neural disorders and enable human augmentation.
analyst_note: Cahira Technologies is positioned at the speculative frontier of nanoelectronic neural interfaces, proposing self-deploying, non-surgical implants that bypass traditional neurosurgical constraints entirely. This approach, if technically viable, would represent a step-change relative to both intracortical and endovascular BCIs, though the company remains at a highly conceptual preclinical stage with significant unanswered questions around targeting precision, safety, and regulatory feasibility.

name: Cala Health
description: Pioneering wearable, wrist-based neuromodulation (TAPS) to reduce essential tremor by delivering patient-specific stimulation to the median and radial nerves.
analyst_note: Cala Health occupies a well-defined niche in peripheral neuromodulation with its wrist-worn TAPS therapy, offering patient-specific stimulation for essential tremor without invasive procedures. With FDA clearance and commercial traction, it sits ahead of most wearable neuromodulation startups, though its indication-specific focus limits platform extensibility compared to broader neuromodulation systems.

name: Cambridge Cognition
description: Providing validated digital cognitive and voice assessments for CNS clinical trials, brain health research, and memory impairment screening.
analyst_note: Cambridge Cognition sits in the established digital neuroassessment layer for CNS research and clinical trial infrastructure. Its position is differentiated by the long-running CANTAB evidence base, public-market status, and expansion into voice and high-frequency digital biomarkers.

name: Cambridge NeuroTech
description: Delivering high-channel-count silicon neural probes and ultra-small headstages enabling artifact-free electrophysiology and optogenetics.
analyst_note: Cambridge NeuroTech is best understood as a next-generation neural interface hardware supplier, competing in the high-channel-count silicon probe market alongside imec and NeuroNexus. Its differentiation lies in ultra-small headstages and artifact-free recording capabilities, though its positioning remains firmly in the research-tools ecosystem rather than clinical translation.

name: Capri Medical
description: Developing an injectable, wireless implantable neurostimulation platform for peripheral nerve modulation, designed to move neuromodulation procedures into outpatient settings.
analyst_note: Capri Medical is targeting a procedural shift in neuromodulation by enabling injectable, wireless implants that move nerve stimulation into outpatient settings, reducing surgical burden. This minimally invasive approach positions it between traditional implantable systems and external wearables, though it remains early-stage with no clinical validation yet.

name: Carthera
description: Developing implantable ultrasound devices that transiently open the blood-brain barrier to support drug delivery for glioblastoma and CNS disorders.
analyst_note: Carthera sits at the interface of focused ultrasound, neuro-oncology, and CNS drug delivery infrastructure. Its SonoCloud platform is differentiated by an implantable BBB-opening approach and a registrational glioblastoma trial, giving it a more clinically advanced profile than most ultrasound delivery platforms.

name: Cefaly
description: Delivering FDA-cleared, over-the-counter external trigeminal nerve stimulation to acutely treat and prevent migraines without drugs.
analyst_note: Cefaly is one of the most commercially established players in consumer-accessible neuromodulation, with OTC trigeminal nerve stimulation for migraine backed by regulatory clearance and direct-to-consumer distribution. Its strong brand and clinical validation create a defensible position, though its modality is limited to a single nerve target compared to broader neuromodulation platforms.

name: Cerca Magnetics
description: Developing a wearable OPM-MEG brain imaging system for non-invasive functional brain mapping across research and clinical neurology.
analyst_note: Cerca Magnetics sits in the emerging OPM-MEG segment, where quantum sensing is being used to make functional brain imaging more adaptable and participant-tolerant. Its positioning is strategically notable because it addresses one of MEG’s core infrastructure constraints: the dependence on large, fixed scanner systems.

name: Cercare Medical
description: Transforming CT and MRI scans into fully automated perfusion maps and advanced microvascular biomarkers to guide stroke and neuro-oncology care.
analyst_note: Cercare Medical is differentiated by its focus on advanced perfusion and microvascular biomarkers derived from standard CT/MRI scans, offering deeper physiological insights than conventional imaging analysis tools. Positioned in stroke and neuro-oncology workflows, it competes with Brainomix and RapidAI but emphasizes proprietary biomarker depth over workflow breadth.

name: Cerebriu
description: Delivering real-time AI-driven MRI workflows, detecting brain infarcts, hemorrhages, and tumors mid-scan to adapt protocols and prioritize urgent cases.
analyst_note: Cerebriu is positioned around real-time, in-scanner AI analysis, enabling adaptive MRI workflows that prioritize urgent findings before scan completion. This intra-scan decision-making capability differentiates it from post-processing imaging software, though adoption depends heavily on integration with existing MRI vendor ecosystems.

name: CereGate
description: Developing a software-driven computer-brain interface platform that augments neuromodulation implants to enable communication and therapy personalization.
analyst_note: CereGate sits in the emerging “software layer for implants” category, augmenting existing neuromodulation devices with communication and adaptive control capabilities rather than developing hardware itself. This platform approach allows it to piggyback on installed DBS infrastructure, though it is dependent on partnerships with device manufacturers for scale.

name: Cerevia Neurosciences
description: Developing a non-invasive fMRI-guided TMS platform for closed-loop neuromodulation in dementia and cognitive impairment.
analyst_note: Cerevia Neurosciences sits in early-stage therapeutic neuromodulation for dementia, combining fMRI-guided targeting, TMS, and adaptive stimulation logic. Its positioning is differentiated by the attempt to bring imaging-informed network modulation into a compact clinical platform for cognitive impairment.

name: Ceribell
description: Developing rapid-response EEG systems and AI software to enable fast detection of seizures and status epilepticus at the point of care.
analyst_note: Ceribell is one of the most commercially successful rapid-EEG companies, with a point-of-care system enabling seizure detection in minutes rather than hours, directly addressing ICU bottlenecks. Its FDA-cleared AI + hardware stack and strong hospital adoption position it as a category leader in acute neurodiagnostics.

name: Charco Neurotech
description: Developing a non-invasive wearable device (CUE1) that uses vibrotactile stimulation to improve motor symptoms in Parkinson’s patients.
analyst_note: Charco Neurotech targets Parkinson’s symptom management via vibrotactile cueing, addressing gait freezing and motor symptoms without invasive intervention. Its wearable-first approach differentiates it from pharmacological and DBS treatments, though clinical efficacy remains under validation relative to established therapies.

name: Cionic
description: Developing an FDA-cleared wearable functional electrical stimulation sleeve that uses sensors and adaptive stimulation to improve gait in neurological mobility impairment.
analyst_note: Cionic is positioned in functional electrical stimulation wearables, with a strong focus on adaptive gait correction using real-time sensor feedback. Its FDA clearance and consumer-friendly sleeve form factor place it ahead of many rehabilitation startups, though it competes with both clinical FES systems and emerging soft robotics solutions.

name: Clarity
description: Developing a non-invasive headset using 40 Hz light and sound stimulation to restore brain rhythms in Alzheimer’s and related disorders
analyst_note: Clarity operates in the growing gamma-stimulation segment for Alzheimer’s, using 40 Hz audiovisual entrainment to target disease-modifying pathways. It sits alongside Cognito Therapeutics but remains earlier-stage, with differentiation primarily around device design and delivery rather than underlying biological mechanism.

name: Clee Medical
description: Developing ultra-high-resolution intraoperative imaging with AI navigation to enable minimally invasive, precise brain surgery.
analyst_note: Clee Medical is positioned in intraoperative imaging and navigation, aiming to improve surgical precision through high-resolution imaging combined with AI guidance. As an early-stage entrant, it competes with established surgical navigation systems but focuses on increasing resolution and minimally invasive applicability.

name: Coapt
description: Developing AI-powered myoelectric control software that enables intuitive, adaptive control of prosthetic limbs.
analyst_note: Coapt is best understood as a software-first prosthetics control company, using pattern-recognition EMG to enable intuitive, adaptive limb control without requiring new hardware. Its acquisition reflects strong validation, and it remains a key enabler layer within the broader prosthetics ecosystem.

name: Cogitat
description: Developing AI-driven EEG decoding software to enable device-agnostic brain-computer interaction and neural signal interpretation.
analyst_note: Cogitat is positioned as a device-agnostic EEG decoding layer, similar to Arctop but with a stronger assistive technology focus in stroke and rehabilitation. Its value lies in abstracting signal interpretation, though differentiation depends on model performance and clinical validation rather than hardware innovation.

name: Cognision
description: Providing an FDA-cleared portable ERP/EEG system for objective assessment of cognitive impairment in dementia, concussion, and TBI.
analyst_note: Cognision occupies a unique position in ERP-based cognitive diagnostics, offering objective EEG-derived metrics rather than subjective cognitive testing. Its FDA clearance provides a regulatory moat, though adoption depends on clinician willingness to integrate EEG into routine assessment workflows.

name: Cognito Therapeutics
description: Evoking gamma brain waves via light and sound headset to slow Alzheimer’s progression, slowing cognitive decline, atrophy, and functional loss.
analyst_note: Cognito Therapeutics is one of the most advanced companies in the gamma entrainment space, with clinical evidence suggesting disease-modifying effects in Alzheimer’s. Its Series C+ funding and clinical progress position it as a leading non-invasive therapeutic contender, though long-term efficacy remains under investigation.

name: Cognixion
description: Empowering communication with a wireless AR headset that blends non-invasive EEG, AI, and augmented reality to help users speak and interact.
analyst_note: Cognixion combines EEG with AR interfaces to create a multimodal communication system for patients with severe motor impairment, positioning it beyond traditional BCIs. Its differentiation lies in integrating interface and decoding into a single product, though it remains early-stage.

name: Cognoa
description: Providing AI-powered tools (Canvas Dx) for rapid, equitable autism diagnosis in young children, and is developing digital therapeutics to improve behavioral health
analyst_note: Cognoa is one of the few FDA-approved digital diagnostic companies in pediatric neurology, with Canvas Dx enabling early autism detection via software. Its regulatory status and clinical validation give it a strong position, though reimbursement and adoption remain key scaling factors.

name: Cogwear
description: Developing EEG-based wearable systems for cognitive performance monitoring in high-demand operational environments including military, aviation, and first responders.
analyst_note: Cogwear occupies the defence and high-stakes operational environment cognitive monitoring niche, differentiating from consumer EEG companies through ruggedised hardware and enterprise/government deployment contexts. This is a commercially viable but niche segment where DARPA and defence agency contracts can provide early revenue without requiring broad clinical adoption.

name: Coherence Neuro
description: Implementing precision bioelectronic therapy with SOMA-1, an implant during glioblastoma surgery that continuously monitors and disrupts tumor-driving electrical signals.
analyst_note: Coherence Neuro sits at the intersection of oncology and neurotechnology, using bioelectronic implants to modulate tumor-associated electrical activity in glioblastoma. This is a highly novel approach with limited precedent, placing it in a high-risk, high-reward translational category.

name: CoMind
description: Developing a non-invasive infrared-based brain monitoring system to provide real-time cerebral perfusion, autoregulation, and intracranial pressure insights in critical care.
analyst_note: CoMind is differentiated by its focus on continuous cerebral hemodynamics monitoring using infrared sensing, targeting ICU and critical care settings. It sits adjacent to invasive ICP monitoring but offers a non-invasive alternative, though clinical validation will determine adoption.

name: Connectoma Neurotech
description: Developing AI- and fMRI-guided TMS protocols for personalized treatment of resistant depression and related psychiatric conditions.
analyst_note: Connectoma Neurotech appears positioned around protocol and targeting personalization rather than proprietary stimulation hardware. Its current placement is early clinical deployment, with public validation still relying more on adjacent accelerated TMS literature than company-specific outcomes.

name: Connectome Health
description: Delivering fast, non-invasive fNIRS brain scans with AI insights to track cognitive focus, memory, resilience, and longevity in real time.
analyst_note: Connectome Health positions itself in consumer fNIRS neuroimaging, translating traditionally lab-bound technology into real-time cognitive metrics for individuals. Its wellness framing expands accessibility but limits clinical credibility and reimbursement pathways.

name: Control Bionics
description: Developing assistive communication technologies that enable individuals with severe physical disabilities to interact with computers and speech-generating devices.
analyst_note: Control Bionics is positioned as a clinically validated assistive communication company leveraging EMG-based interfaces to enable interaction for patients with severe motor impairment. Its FDA-cleared systems and long operating history place it among the more mature players in non-invasive assistive neurotech, though its technology is evolutionary rather than paradigm-shifting.

name: Cordance Medical
description: Developing a non-invasive focused ultrasound platform to precisely open the blood–brain barrier and enable targeted drug delivery and brain diagnostics.
analyst_note: Cordance Medical sits in the emerging focused ultrasound segment targeting blood–brain barrier opening for drug delivery, a modality gaining traction in oncology and neurology. Its differentiation lies in combining therapeutic delivery with potential diagnostic applications, though it remains early-stage relative to more established ultrasound players like Insightec.

name: CorTec
description: Building a fully implantable, bidirectional neurostimulation and recording platform designed to restore neural function by sensing brain activity and delivering adaptive stimulation in closed loop.
analyst_note: CorTec is developing a fully implantable closed-loop neurostimulation platform, positioning itself as a next-generation alternative to traditional DBS systems with integrated sensing and adaptive stimulation. Its bidirectional architecture aligns with the broader shift toward closed-loop neuromodulation, though commercialization timelines remain unclear.

name: Cortical Labs
description: Developing the CL1 'biocomputer', a silicon-embedded, lab-grown neuron platform (SBI) that learns via real-time neural code execution.
analyst_note: Cortical Labs is best understood as a frontier “biocomputing” company, combining living neurons with silicon hardware to create hybrid computational systems. While scientifically novel, its commercial applications remain exploratory, positioning it more as research infrastructure than a near-term product company.

name: Corticale
description: Developing minimally invasive CMOS-based cortical implants (SiNAPS) that record from thousands of neurons for high-resolution brain-computer interfaces.
analyst_note: Corticale is developing high-density cortical implants using CMOS technology to achieve large-scale neural recording with minimal invasiveness. It sits in the next-generation ECoG BCI category alongside Precision Neuroscience, though still at an early translational stage.

name: CortiVision
description: Enabling mobile, high-density fNIRS brain imaging, used from labs to the ISS, tracking brain activity via oxygenation, multimodal interactions, and hyperscanning.
analyst_note: CortiVision is positioned as a high-density fNIRS hardware provider, enabling portable, research-grade brain imaging in real-world environments. Its differentiation lies in spatial resolution and portability, though it remains squarely in the research-tools market rather than clinical deployment.

name: CraniUS Therapeutics
description: Developing a skull-embedded, pump-driven intracranial drug delivery platform designed for repeatable, targeted convection-enhanced infusion beyond the blood-brain barrier.
analyst_note: CraniUS Therapeutics targets a specific bottleneck in CNS drug delivery with its implantable convection-enhanced delivery system, enabling repeated, localized dosing beyond the blood–brain barrier. This positions it as enabling infrastructure for neuro-oncology therapies rather than a standalone therapeutic company.

name: CTRL-labs (Meta)
description: Built a neural-interface wristband decoding hand-movement intent via sEMG, paving the way for gesture-free device control and AR/VR input (acquired by Meta).
analyst_note: CTRL-labs, now part of Meta, pioneered non-invasive EMG-based neural interfaces for gesture-free control, effectively creating a new input paradigm for AR/VR. Its acquisition validates peripheral neural interfaces as a strategic layer in human–computer interaction.

name: Cumulus Neuroscience
description: Developing a wearable EEG and digital biomarker platform to enable remote, objective measurement of brain function in clinical trials and neuroscience research.
analyst_note: Cumulus Neuroscience is positioned as a pharma-facing EEG biomarker platform, enabling remote and scalable CNS data collection for clinical trials. Its FDA-cleared headset and focus on decentralized trials align with broader shifts in clinical research infrastructure.

name: Curonix
description: Developing StimRouter, a minimally invasive peripheral nerve stimulation system with an implantable lead and externally worn wireless pulse transmitter for chronic pain treatment.
analyst_note: Curonix's StimRouter occupies the minimally invasive implantable PNS segment alongside SPR Therapeutics, with a wirelessly powered architecture that reduces the implant burden relative to fully independent battery-powered systems. Its FDA clearance across multiple chronic pain anatomical locations gives it broad applicability, though commercial traction requires overcoming physician familiarity with conventional SCS platforms.

name: Dandelion Science
description: Developing a generative AI-driven neuromodulation platform for non-invasive programmable neurotherapeutics targeting brain disorders.
analyst_note: Dandelion Science sits at the intersection of AI and neuromodulation, proposing programmable, software-defined neurotherapeutics delivered non-invasively. While conceptually compelling, it remains preclinical and dependent on demonstrating that software-layer optimization meaningfully improves outcomes.

name: DEEGtal
description: Delivering an AI-driven platform that enhances traditional EEG analysis by uncovering complex, visually silent patterns, enabling faster, more accurate epilepsy diagnoses.
analyst_note: dEEGtal is positioned as an AI augmentation layer for EEG interpretation, focusing on uncovering subtle patterns missed by human review in epilepsy diagnostics. It competes in a crowded clinical AI space where differentiation depends heavily on validation and integration into workflows.

name: Deep Sleep Technologies
description: Developing closed-loop, brainwave-synchronized acoustic neurostimulation technology designed to enhance deep sleep and reduce daytime fatigue.
analyst_note: The company licenses its stimulation layer into existing wearables rather than shipping its own headband, a distribution choice that trades hardware margins for faster reach into Oura's and Apple's installed base. University of Amsterdam origins and a decade of underlying sleep research give it more scientific weight than most consumer sleep-tech entrants carry.

name: DeepSpin
description: Building portable, affordable AI-powered MRI systems, delivering high-quality brain imaging at 20× lower cost, weight, and infrastructure needs.
analyst_note: DeepSpin aims to radically reduce MRI cost and infrastructure through portable, AI-enhanced systems, positioning itself as a disruptive entrant in neuroimaging hardware. If successful, it could expand access significantly, though it faces substantial technical and regulatory hurdles.

name: Earable Neuroscience
description: Delivering a smart EEG brainband that tracks sleep, focus, and bio-signals in real time, and uses AI-driven audio feedback to enhance sleep and cognition.
analyst_note: Earable Neuroscience is positioned in the consumer EEG wearable space with an emphasis on sleep and cognitive enhancement via real-time feedback. Its differentiation lies in combining sensing with audio-based intervention, though it remains in the wellness category.

name: Eightsix Science
description: Developing biohybrid brain tissue grafts made through advanced bioprinting to restore brain function and enable direct interfacing with neural circuits.
analyst_note: Eightsix Science is pursuing biohybrid tissue grafts for brain repair, placing it at the intersection of regenerative medicine, bioprinting, and neural interfacing. This is a scientifically ambitious infrastructure-and-therapy hybrid that remains firmly preclinical.

name: ELDA BrainTech
description: Combining MRI-compatible EEG cap with AI to pinpoint epileptic zones via simultaneous EEG–fMRI recordings, improving diagnosis precision.
analyst_note: ELDA BrainTech is developing combined EEG–fMRI analysis tools for epilepsy localization, targeting improved diagnostic precision in surgical planning. Its multimodal approach offers higher accuracy than single-modality systems but increases complexity and cost.

name: ElectroCore
description: Developing gammaCore, an FDA-cleared non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation handheld device for the treatment of migraine, cluster headache, and other neurological conditions.
analyst_note: electroCore is the most commercially advanced non-invasive VNS company, holding the first FDA clearance for neck-based transcutaneous VNS and a broad migraine/cluster headache indication set with reimbursement in some settings. Its public market status and military partnerships give it a distinctive commercial profile in the growing neuromodulation headache space.

name: Elemind
description: Developing an EEG headband that uses adaptive acoustic stimulation to support faster sleep onset and consumer sleep improvement.
analyst_note: Elemind sits in the consumer sleep neurotechnology segment, where EEG is used as an input for active sleep intervention. Its positioning is differentiated by closed-loop acoustic stimulation, placing it between consumer sleep wearables and more technically involved neurofeedback systems.

name: EMOTIV
description: Offering wireless, multi-channel EEG headsets and SDKs, empowering BCI research, emotion tracking, and hands-free control across diverse applications.
analyst_note: EMOTIV is one of the most established consumer/research EEG hardware companies, offering accessible headsets with a strong developer ecosystem. Its longevity and brand recognition are key advantages, though it operates primarily outside clinical markets.

name: Empatica
description: Developing medical-grade wearable sensors and analytics to enable remote monitoring and detection of neurological and physiological events.
analyst_note: Empatica is a leading player in medical-grade wearables, with FDA-cleared devices for seizure detection and physiological monitoring. Its strong clinical validation and pharma partnerships position it at the intersection of digital health and neurotech.

name: Emteq Labs
description: Developing AI-powered emotion-sensing eyewear that captures facial muscle activity for health and behavioral insights.
analyst_note: Emteq Labs focuses on emotion-sensing via facial EMG embedded in wearable devices, targeting behavioral analytics and affective computing. Its positioning is adjacent to neurotech but more aligned with human–computer interaction and XR applications.

name: EMVision
description: Developing portable electromagnetic brain imaging systems to enable rapid, point-of-care diagnosis of stroke and other acute neurological conditions.
analyst_note: EMVision is developing portable electromagnetic imaging for stroke diagnosis, offering a radiation-free alternative to CT. Its point-of-care focus targets emergency settings, though it remains in the investigational stage.

name: Encora Therapeutics
description: Developing non-invasive neuromodulation therapies targeting peripheral nerves to treat chronic neurological conditions such as essential tremor.
analyst_note: Encora Therapeutics is positioned in peripheral neuromodulation for movement disorders, particularly essential tremor. Its non-invasive approach competes with Cala Health but remains earlier in clinical validation.

name: eNeura
description: Providing FDA-cleared single-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation devices for acute and preventive migraine treatment at home.
analyst_note: eNeura sits in prescription home-use neuromodulation for migraine, with sTMS as a central stimulation approach distinct from peripheral nerve stimulation peers. Its profile is more mature than most migraine-device startups, with FDA-cleared indications and a long commercialization history.

name: Enspire DBS
description: Developing an implantable deep brain stimulation system combined with rehabilitation therapy to restore arm motor function after stroke.
analyst_note: Enspire's DBS+Rehab approach targets the dentate nucleus rather than the more commonly stimulated basal ganglia targets used in movement disorders, extending DBS into stroke motor recovery, a largely untapped indication for the modality. Its EDEN trial results published in Nature Medicine and ongoing FDA IDE-approved RESTORE pivotal study place it further along the regulatory path than most stroke neuromodulation companies, backed by a Cleveland Clinic origin and continued institutional financing.

name: Epia Neuro
description: Developing minimally invasive brain-computer interfaces that decode motor intent and pair neural sensing with stimulation to restore function after stroke.
analyst_note: Epia neuro has minimal public information available, making detailed competitive analysis difficult. Based on the domain name and URL, the company appears to operate in the epilepsy diagnostics or monitoring space, placing it adjacent to Ceribell and Epitel, though the specific modality, form factor, and regulatory stage remain undisclosed.

name: Epiminder
description: Developing an implantable seizure monitoring system to provide continuous, objective tracking of epileptic activity over long durations.
analyst_note: Epiminder is developing implantable, long-term EEG monitoring systems, enabling continuous seizure tracking beyond hospital settings. This positions it as infrastructure for epilepsy management rather than a therapeutic solution.

name: Epitel
description: Developing wearable, long-term EEG monitoring systems to enable continuous seizure detection and neurological assessment outside the hospital.
analyst_note: Epitel focuses on wearable, long-duration EEG monitoring using adhesive sensors, improving patient comfort and accessibility compared to traditional systems. Its FDA clearance supports adoption in outpatient neurology.

name: EpiWatch
description: Developing an Apple Watch-based seizure detection and alerting application for epilepsy patients, enabling wrist-worn smartwatch monitoring for tonic-clonic seizures.
analyst_note: EpiWatch occupies a distinctive niche as an Apple Watch-native seizure detection app, leveraging consumer hardware to provide passive monitoring without requiring dedicated medical wearables. Its FDA clearance and Johns Hopkins collaboration lend credibility, though tonic-clonic seizure detection sensitivity on wrist accelerometry is lower than EEG-based systems, limiting its use to a specific patient population.

name: EVOCAL Health
description: Unlocking voice as a predictive biomarker using AI to detect diseases and support digital diagnostics and therapies across Longevity and neurodegeneration.
analyst_note: EVOCAL Health operates in the voice biomarker space, targeting longevity and neurodegeneration through speech analysis. Its positioning overlaps with multiple competitors, with differentiation dependent on dataset quality and partnerships.

name: Eysz
description: Developing eye-tracking–based neuroassessment software to objectively detect and monitor concussion and brain injury.
analyst_note: Eysz uses eye-tracking as a digital biomarker for neurological conditions, particularly concussion. Its non-invasive, software-based approach enables scalable screening but faces competition from other digital assessment tools.

name: Farow
description: Developing a wearable-based seizure detection system to monitor nocturnal epileptic seizures in children using passive physiological signals.
analyst_note: Farow focuses on pediatric epilepsy monitoring using wearable sensors for nocturnal seizure detection. Its niche focus on children and home monitoring differentiates it from broader EEG platforms.

name: FinalSpark
description: Operating the first remotely accessible biocomputing research platform using living human brain organoids on multi-electrode arrays as computational substrates.
analyst_note: FinalSpark is the most operationally distinctive biocomputing company, having built the only remotely accessible organoid computing platform with a subscriber base across ten universities. Its differentiation lies in infrastructure democratization rather than proprietary science, making it closer to cloud-lab infrastructure for wetware research than a product company with defined clinical or commercial endpoints.

name: Firefly Neuroscience
description: Developing EEG-based brain network analytics software to support objective assessment of neurological and psychiatric conditions.
analyst_note: Firefly Neuroscience provides EEG-based brain network analytics, translating raw signals into clinically meaningful biomarkers. Its FDA clearance strengthens its position in psychiatric and neurological assessment.

name: Fisher Wallace Labs
description: Offering an FDA-cleared cranial electrotherapy stimulator that non-invasively treats depression, anxiety, and insomnia via home use.
analyst_note: Fisher Wallace Labs is a long-standing player in cranial electrotherapy stimulation, offering home-use devices for depression and anxiety. Its regulatory pathway and consumer accessibility drive adoption, though clinical efficacy debates persist.

name: FlectoThink
description: Developing a flexible EEG sleep patch for non-invasive brain monitoring, sleep-stage assessment, and consumer BCI applications.
analyst_note: FlectoThink sits in the flexible EEG segment of consumer neurotechnology, with sleep monitoring as the clearest near-term product application. Its positioning is differentiated by the use of a lightweight forehead patch, giving it a lower-burden alternative to headband and earbud-based EEG systems.

name: Flourish
description: Building brain-inspired AI architectures that study cortical circuits and connectomics to improve computational efficiency and continuous learning.
analyst_note: Neuroscience here serves as an architectural blueprint for AI hardware, not a tool for interfacing with human neural activity, which puts Flourish adjacent to the neurotech landscape rather than inside it. It's worth tracking as a neuroscience-to-computing crossover, seen also in new entrants like The Biological Computing Co.

name: Flow Neuroscience
description: Delivering a portable tDCS headset that gently stimulates the prefrontal cortex to relieve depression symptoms, med-free, at-home therapy.
analyst_note: Flow Neuroscience combines tDCS with behavioral therapy in a consumer-friendly format for depression treatment. Its FDA approval and integrated app ecosystem position it as a scalable alternative to pharmacotherapy.

name: Fluent
description: Developing non-invasive brain-computer interfaces that translate neural intent into fluid, real-time control for communication and interaction.
analyst_note: Fluent BCI is developing implantable communication-focused BCIs, targeting high-fidelity neural decoding for real-time interaction. It remains at an early, preclinical stage in a highly competitive space.

name: Forest Neurotech
description: Pioneering ultrasound-based brain–computer interfaces using Forest 1, a compact, fob-sized scanner enabling noninvasive whole-brain imaging and neuromodulation.
analyst_note: Forest Neurotech is exploring ultrasound-based whole-brain interfaces, combining imaging and stimulation in a compact form factor. Its approach is highly ambitious but remains research-focused.

name: G.tec
description: Developing non-invasive and invasive EEG-based systems for brain-computer interface research, neuroimaging, and clinical neuroscience applications.
analyst_note: G.tec is one of the most established providers of EEG and BCI systems for research and clinical use, with a strong reputation in high-performance signal acquisition. It serves as a benchmark provider in the academic neurotech ecosystem.

name: General Sense
description: Developing neural sensing systems that decode odor-related brain activity in animals to support scent detection across security, inspection, and research settings.
analyst_note: General Sense is perhaps the first commercial animal-machine interface company, using neural decoding of canine olfaction as a sensing layer for chemical detection. Its positioning stands out by treating the trained dog less as a behavioral detector and more as a biological front end for deployable sensing infrastructure across security, healthcare, and agricultural contexts.

name: Gestala
description: Building a non-invasive ultrasound-based brain-computer interface platform for neuromodulation and neural signal decoding.
analyst_note: Gestala is developing ultrasound-based BCIs, aiming to combine non-invasive stimulation with neural decoding. It sits in an early-stage, experimental category alongside other ultrasound neurotech startups.

name: Gowerlabs
description: Delivering wearable, high-density fNIRS systems (LUMO & NTS) for 3D brain imaging in infants and adults across research and clinical settings globally.
analyst_note: Gowerlabs is a leading provider of high-density fNIRS systems, particularly in developmental neuroscience and infant studies. Its hardware is widely adopted in research settings but not yet positioned for clinical use.

name: GrayMatters Health
description: Developing Prism, an FDA-cleared neurofeedback system using EEG-based biomarkers to train self-regulation of brain networks in PTSD and depression.
analyst_note: GrayMatters Health is positioned in neurofeedback therapeutics, with FDA-cleared software targeting PTSD and depression through brain network self-regulation. Its clinical validation differentiates it from wellness-focused neurofeedback platforms.

name: Great Lakes NeuroTech
description: Developing EEG-based neuroimaging and brain-computer interface software for neuroscience research and clinical applications.
analyst_note: Great Lakes NeuroTech provides EEG-based tools and software for research and clinical use, focusing on usability and workflow integration. It operates in a crowded but stable research-tools market.

name: Grey Matter Neurosciences
description: Developing portable, focused ultrasound headset to non‑invasively stimulate deep brain circuits and improve cognition in Alzheimer’s disease.
analyst_note: Grey Matter Neurosciences is developing focused ultrasound neuromodulation for Alzheimer’s, targeting deep brain circuits non-invasively. It remains early-stage but aligned with a growing interest in ultrasound therapies.

name: Halo Neuroscience
description: Developing non-invasive transcranial direct current stimulation devices to enhance motor learning and neuroplasticity.
analyst_note: Halo Neuroscience was positioned in the consumer neurostimulation segment, using tDCS to enhance motor learning and athletic performance rather than treating disease. Its acquisition and product focus placed it closer to performance technology than clinical neurotherapy, limiting regulatory complexity but also constraining medical defensibility.

name: Hemispheric
description: Building a large-scale EEG foundation model that decodes brain activity to support objective diagnosis and treatment selection for neuropsychiatric conditions.
analyst_note: A six-billion-parameter EEG foundation model trained across 250,000 hours of data is a scale bet few diagnostics companies can match, aiming to generalize across PTSD, depression, and neurodegenerative conditions from one underlying platform. Six years in stealth and a $52M raise suggest serious institutional conviction, clinical and regulatory validation are next.

name: Hyperfine
description: Providing the first FDA-cleared portable, ultra-low-field MRI system for point-of-care brain imaging in hospitals, clinics, and emergency settings.
analyst_note: Hyperfine has moved past the validation question that most portable imaging entrants face, its Swoop system is generating recurring revenue (45% year-over-year growth) and record U.S. scan volumes rather than pilot-stage adoption. Recent CE marking and a European commercial launch mark a company scaling an already-cleared product internationally, a later stage of maturity than most companies in this category.

name: i-BrainTech
description: Providing EEG-based BCI neurofeedback training for motor imagery, sports performance, cognitive assessment, and rehabilitation workflows.
analyst_note: i-BrainTech sits at the edge of sports neurotechnology and rehabilitation BCI, using EEG feedback to make motor imagery training measurable. Its strongest public traction appears to be elite-sports deployment, while medical-device status and company-specific clinical validation remain less clearly documented.

name: Icometrix
description: Developing AI-powered neuroimaging software to quantify brain structures and pathology for clinical decision support and research.
analyst_note: Icometrix is one of the more established clinical neuroimaging software companies, providing automated quantification of brain structure and pathology for diseases such as MS, dementia, and traumatic injury. Its FDA-cleared footprint and acquisition support position it as a mature workflow-integration player rather than a novel biomarker startup.

name: ICONEUS
description: Developing functional ultrasound neuroimaging systems to enable high-resolution, real-time imaging of brain activity in research and clinical settings.
analyst_note: ICONEUS occupies a highly differentiated niche in functional ultrasound imaging, enabling real-time brain activity mapping with temporal and spatial resolution beyond what most portable modalities can offer. Despite the technical strength of the platform, it remains primarily a research-market company rather than a clinically deployed neuroimaging business.

name: IDUN Technologies
description: Developing discreet in-ear EEG sensors and neuroanalytics to transform everyday wearables into continuous brain-state monitoring tools.
analyst_note: IDUN Technologies is positioned around in-ear EEG as an enabling layer for everyday brain-state sensing, offering a more discreet form factor than headbands or caps. Its developer-oriented strategy places it in the infrastructure tier of wearable neurotech, with differentiation driven by usability and integration potential rather than clinical validation.

name: Imeka
description: Developing AI-driven neuroimaging software to analyze diffusion MRI data for improved diagnosis and monitoring of neurological disorders.
analyst_note: Imeka sits in the diffusion MRI analytics market, offering software that extracts clinically useful microstructural biomarkers from complex imaging datasets. Its value proposition is strongest in turning high-dimensional diffusion data into decision-support outputs, though it competes in a specialist segment with relatively long sales cycles.

name: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics
description: Developing ultrathin graphene-based neural implants (<10 µm) for AI-powered, bidirectional modulation of neurological disorders like Parkinson’s.
analyst_note: INBRAIN Neuroelectrics is differentiated by its graphene-based implant architecture, which promises thinner, more conformable, and potentially higher-fidelity neural interfaces than conventional materials. Its Series B funding and therapeutic focus in Parkinson’s and epilepsy position it among the more credible next-generation implantable neuroelectronics companies, though it remains pre-commercial.

name: Inner Cosmos
description: Developing an implantable digital neuromodulation system to deliver precision brain stimulation for the treatment of depression.
analyst_note: Inner Cosmos is pursuing a minimally invasive implantable neuromodulation system for depression, effectively bringing a psychiatry indication into a category more commonly associated with movement disorders or epilepsy. The company’s differentiation lies in applying digital precision-stimulation concepts to mental health, though it remains early relative to established psychiatric neuromodulation platforms.

name: Insai
description: Developing AI foundation models that turn sleep and EEG data into objective biomarkers for research, pharma, and clinical development.
analyst_note: Insai is best understood as a research-oriented closed-loop neuromodulation platform combining sensing and low-intensity magnetic stimulation in a wearable format. Its pharma-facing positioning suggests infrastructure for experimentation and biomarker generation rather than a patient-ready therapeutic business.

name: Insellar
description: Developing a minimally invasive brain interface for treatment-resistant depression by targeting endogenous hormone-release pathways.
analyst_note: Insellar sits at the edge of psychiatric neuromodulation and bioelectronic medicine, using a minimally invasive interface concept to engage endogenous hormone-release pathways in treatment-resistant depression. Its positioning is notable for linking neuroendocrine modulation with severe psychiatry at a preclinical stage.

name: Inspire Medical Systems
description: Providing an implantable hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy for obstructive sleep apnea in patients unable to use CPAP.
analyst_note: Inspire Medical Systems sits in one of the most commercially mature segments of implantable neuromodulation, with hypoglossal nerve stimulation established as a regulated therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. Its positioning is strategically notable because it connects sleep medicine, surgical implantation, and closed-loop peripheral nerve stimulation in a narrowly defined clinical market.

name: Intactis Bio
description: Developing biohybrid computing systems that use living neural tissue and silicon interfaces for low-energy AI/ML workloads.
analyst_note: Intactis Bio sits closer to biohybrid computing infrastructure than clinical neurotechnology, using cultured neurons as a processing layer. Its current profile is early and experimental, with public materials focused on Alpha access, grant support, and initial demonstrations.

name: Iota Biosciences
description: Developing ultra-miniaturized, wirelessly powered implantable bioelectronic devices that use ultrasonic power and communication for minimally invasive neuromodulation.
analyst_note: iota Biosciences is differentiated by its ultrasonic powering architecture for sub-millimeter implants, a technically compelling approach that eliminates batteries and reduces implant size to needle-injectable dimensions. As an Astellas acquisition, it is best understood as pharma-enabling bioelectronic infrastructure rather than an independent device company pursuing its own commercial pathway.

name: Kandu
description: Developing a tech-enabled post-acute stroke care platform that combines navigation services, telehealth, and digital tools to support recovery after hospital discharge
analyst_note: Kandu occupies the post-acute stroke recovery software segment, focusing on care coordination, monitoring, and digital support rather than a novel neurotechnology modality. Its strength is workflow and patient-management integration, though its differentiation is less technical than companies building proprietary hardware or biomarkers.

name: Karavela AI
description: Building an AI-based “foundation model” of brain activity from large fMRI datasets to enable new neurological diagnostics and biomarkers.
analyst_note: Karavela AI is positioned as a brain-foundation-model company, aiming to build large-scale representations of brain activity from fMRI datasets. This places it in the emerging AI-infrastructure layer for neuroscience, where differentiation depends less on a single product and more on proprietary data access and model performance.

name: Kernel
description: Providing fNIRS neuroimaging (Flow) for high-density brain monitoring targeting research and potential BCI applications in cognition and health.
analyst_note: Kernel has been one of the highest-profile entrants in non-invasive neuroimaging, translating high-density fNIRS into a polished research platform with ambitions spanning cognition, health, and future interface applications. Its differentiation lies in engineering quality and brand visibility, though commercial traction has been concentrated in research rather than clinical markets.

name: Kinesix XR
description: Delivering immersive AI‑driven VR/AR therapy platform offering personalized neurorehabilitation exercises to improve motor and cognitive recovery.
analyst_note: Kinesix XR sits in the neurorehabilitation software segment, combining VR/AR delivery with AI-personalized therapeutic exercises for motor and cognitive recovery. Its approach is scalable and accessible, though it competes in a crowded digital-therapy category where reimbursement and clinical validation are critical.

name: Kneu Health
description: Developing a wearable and software platform to monitor neurological function and recovery using objective movement and physiological data.
analyst_note: Kneu Health is positioned around objective neurological monitoring through wearable and software-based data capture, targeting recovery and disease progression tracking. Its promise lies in digitizing longitudinal neurological assessment, though its competitive moat appears more workflow-based than modality-driven.

name: Koniku
description: Developing wetware neuron-silicon hybrid chips that use engineered biological neurons with olfactory receptors for chemical detection and sensing applications.
analyst_note: Koniku occupies a highly distinctive position as a wetware company using living neurons as biological sensors for chemical detection, setting it apart from conventional neural interface or imaging companies. Its commercial partnerships with Airbus and security deployments at SFO make it one of the few biocomputing companies with real-world validated hardware, though its neurotech classification is more adjacent to biosensing than brain-computer interfaces.

name: Kyma Neuro
description: Developing a modular non-invasive BCI headset and developer platform for building software controlled by neural signals.
analyst_note: Kyma Neuro appears positioned as a developer-first non-invasive BCI platform, combining low-cost sensing hardware with APIs, models, and application tooling. Its current status is very early, with public materials centered on a planned 2026 developer-kit release rather than validated applications or regulated clinical use.

name: Linus Health
description: Developing digital cognitive assessment and decision-support tools to enable earlier detection and management of neurodegenerative disease.
analyst_note: Linus Health is one of the more commercially advanced digital cognitive assessment platforms, combining validated tests, decision support, and acquired biomarker capabilities such as speech analytics. Its positioning is strongest as a clinician-facing dementia workflow platform rather than a breakthrough biomarker company.

name: Longeviti Neuro Solutions
description: Developing ultrasound-based neuroimaging platforms to enable real-time brain imaging during and after complex neurosurgical procedures.
