analyst_note: Longeviti Neuro Solutions occupies a differentiated position in neurosurgical imaging, using ultrasound-based platforms for real-time intraoperative and perioperative brain visualization. This makes it enabling infrastructure for complex procedures rather than a general neurodiagnostics company.

name: Looxid Labs
description: Developing wearable eye-tracking and EEG biometric sensor solutions integrated with XR headsets to capture cognitive and emotional data for enterprise and research applications.
analyst_note: Looxid Labs occupies the XR-embedded biometrics niche, differentiating from standalone EEG platforms by combining eye-tracking and neural sensing within VR headsets. This is a compelling integration for enterprise and research applications where immersive context and cognitive measurement are both required, though it is dependent on the growth trajectory of enterprise VR adoption.

name: LYEONS Neurotech
description: Developing wearable EEG monitoring and neurofeedback solutions for cognitive performance enhancement and mental health applications.
analyst_note: LYEONS Neurotech is an early-stage consumer EEG platform competing in a heavily commoditised segment. With minimal public information, it is difficult to assess differentiation, and its commercial viability will depend on hardware quality, form factor design, and developer ecosystem development.

name: Machine Medicine
description: Providing AI-powered video assessment of Parkinson’s motor symptoms, offering objective, reproducible metrics for clinical trials and care.
analyst_note: Machine Medicine is best understood as an objective digital phenotyping company for movement disorders, using computer vision and AI to quantify Parkinson’s symptoms for care and clinical trials. Its strength lies in reproducibility and trial utility, though it remains closer to biomarker infrastructure than therapeutics.

name: MachineMD
description: Developing a VR-based neuro-ophthalmology device that automatically measures eye and pupil responses to detect neurological disorders early.
analyst_note: MachineMD is differentiated by its VR-based neuro-ophthalmology platform, automating eye and pupil testing in a way that can reveal neurological dysfunction earlier and more consistently than manual exams. Its CE-marked position gives it a clearer clinical pathway than many digital neurodiagnostics startups.

name: Magnetic Tides
description: Developing a non-invasive kTMP brain stimulation platform for stroke motor recovery and neurological or psychiatric applications.
analyst_note: Magnetic Tides sits in the non-invasive brain stimulation segment, with kTMP positioned as a technical extension of the TMS and electrical-stimulation design space. Its relevance comes from targeting chronic stroke motor recovery with a stimulation approach built around frequency-specific, spatially targeted cortical modulation.

name: Magnus Medical
description: Developing SAINT®, an image-guided, accelerated, non-invasive neuromodulation system targeting personalized brain networks to treat severe depression.
analyst_note: Magnus Medical sits at the high end of psychiatric neuromodulation, commercializing accelerated, image-guided TMS based on the SAINT protocol for severe depression. Its PMA-level approval and strong Stanford-derived clinical narrative position it as one of the most clinically credible next-generation TMS companies.

name: Mainstay Medical
description: Developing the ReActiv8 restorative neurostimulation system, an implantable device that stimulates lumbas nerves to treat chronic mechanical low back pain.
analyst_note: Mainstay Medical is the most commercially advanced company in restorative neurostimulation for mechanical low back pain, a mechanistically distinct category from conventional SCS that targets the underlying multifidus dysfunction rather than pain signal masking. Its public status, two-year RCT data, and FDA approval give it a significant head start, though reimbursement access remains a key adoption constraint in the US market.

name: Manava Plus
description: Developing implantable neural prostheses for spinal cord injury that aim to reconnect damaged pathways and restore motor and sensory function.
analyst_note: Manava Plus is developing implantable spinal neuroprostheses for spinal cord injury, targeting restoration of motor and sensory pathways rather than symptomatic management alone. This places it in the restorative neurotechnology segment, though still at an early preclinical stage.

name: Marbles Health
description: Offering portable, hospital‑grade non‑invasive neuromodulation (tES + EEG + cognitive training) to support recovery from mental health and neuropsychiatric conditions.
analyst_note: Marbles Health combines tES, EEG, and cognitive training into a portable mental-health platform, positioning itself as a hybrid between neuromodulation device and digital therapeutic. Its breadth is appealing, but also risks diluting differentiation unless one component clearly drives outcomes.

name: Mave Health
description: Developing a non-invasive tDCS-based brain stimulation platform aimed at improving focus, stress regulation, emotional control, and sleep by targeting prefrontal cortex function.
analyst_note: Mave sits in the consumer tDCS wellness category, targeting focus, stress regulation, emotional control, and sleep through prefrontal stimulation. It is best understood as a lifestyle neurostimulation product rather than a regulated mental-health therapy.

name: MaxWell Biosystems
description: Delivering high-density microelectrode array platforms that record and stimulate neural cells in vitro, accelerating neuroscience and drug discovery.
analyst_note: MaxWell Biosystems is a direct peer to 3Brain in the high-density MEA market, supplying ex vivo electrophysiology tools for neuroscience and drug discovery. Its differentiation lies in cell-level recording and stimulation performance, making it infrastructure for pharma and research rather than a translational neurotech company.

name: Mendi
description: Offering a portable fNIRS-based neurofeedback headband and app to help users train their prefrontal cortex for improved focus, stress relief, and mood.
analyst_note: Mendi sits in the consumer fNIRS neurofeedback segment, translating a traditionally research-bound imaging modality into an accessible wellness product focused on focus and stress. Its differentiation is primarily the modality itself, though the consumer framing limits clinical claims.

name: Merge Labs
description: Exploring gene-therapy-enhanced, high-bandwidth, ultrasound-based brain-computer interfaces to enable seamless human–AI integration.
analyst_note: Merge Labs represents a highly speculative attempt to combine ultrasound BCI concepts with gene-therapy-style enhancement and human–AI integration narratives. It is best viewed as frontier research ambition rather than a near-term commercial neurotechnology company.

name: MindAffect
description: Providing EEG-based neurofeedback and brain training solutions to support mental health and cognitive regulation.
analyst_note: MindAffect operates in the EEG neurofeedback and brain-training segment, targeting cognitive regulation and mental wellbeing. Its challenge is standing out in a category crowded with neurofeedback offerings, where differentiation often depends more on engagement and evidence than underlying sensing technology.

name: MindMuscle
description: Building wearable EEG + AI-powered neurofeedback platform for children with ADHD/ASD to improve attention and learning without medication.
analyst_note: PigPug Health combines EEG and AI neurofeedback for pediatric attention and learning support, positioning itself in the child-focused digital mental-health segment. Its challenge will be standing out in a category where engagement, evidence, and reimbursement all matter.

name: MindRove
description: Offering wearable EEG and EMG biosensing devices and SDK for neural interface development, neurofeedback, rehabilitation, and research applications.
analyst_note: MindRove is positioned as an accessible EEG/EMG hardware-and-SDK provider, enabling developers and researchers to prototype neural-interface applications without premium system costs. It occupies the lower-cost infrastructure tier rather than the clinical or high-performance research end of the market.

name: MintNeuro
description: Developing ultra-efficient semiconductor chips that shrink and power neural implants, enabling scalable, minimally invasive brain therapies.
analyst_note: MintNeuro is best understood as deep-tech semiconductor infrastructure for neurotechnology, focusing on power-efficient chips that could shrink and scale implants. This is a valuable but upstream position in the stack, making it more comparable to component suppliers than device companies.

name: MJN Neuroserveis
description: Developing a wearable earpiece sensor (mjn-SERAS) that uses EEG and AI to predict epileptic seizures and warn patients in advance.
analyst_note: MJN Neuroserveis is differentiated by its earpiece-based seizure forecasting system, which aims to predict rather than merely detect epileptic events. That predictive ambition is strategically attractive, though commercial success depends on reliability in real-world use and clinician trust.

name: Mobia Medical
description: Developing implantable paired vagus nerve stimulation systems to support upper-limb rehabilitation in chronic ischemic stroke survivors.
analyst_note: Mobia Medical is positioned around paired neurostimulation and rehabilitation rather than stimulation as a standalone intervention. Its Vivistim system gives it a relatively mature commercial profile within stroke neurorecovery, with PMA approval and public-market access.

name: Mon4t
description: Transforming standard smartphones into AI-powered neurological test devices for remote motor, cognitive, and affective monitoring.
analyst_note: Mon4t turns commodity smartphones into neurological assessment devices, making it a software-first digital biomarker platform for remote monitoring of motor and cognitive status. Its strongest advantage is accessibility and low deployment friction, though this also lowers barriers to imitation.

name: Morph Labs
description: Building brain-driven prosthetic control via AI-decoded neural signals, translating amputees’ brainwaves into intuitive limb movement.
analyst_note: Morph Labs is pursuing non-invasive prosthetic control through AI-decoded brain signals, positioning itself in the assistive BCI space without implants. This is a compelling accessibility angle, though it competes against EMG-based and invasive approaches with clearer near-term performance benchmarks.

name: Motif Neurotech
description: Developing minimally invasive, battery-free brain implants (DOT) that wirelessly stimulate brain circuits to treat treatment-resistant depression.
analyst_note: Motif Neurotech is differentiated by its tiny, battery-free, minimally invasive implant architecture for depression, targeting a gap between external psychiatric neuromodulation and larger implanted systems. Its hardware elegance is a strong narrative advantage, though clinical proof remains early.

name: Muse
description: Empowering meditation and mental fitness with wearable EEG headbands (Muse) that deliver real-time neurofeedback for focus, relaxation, and sleep.
analyst_note: Muse is one of the most recognizable consumer EEG brands, using neurofeedback to support meditation, sleep, and mental fitness. Its differentiation is less about raw sensing sophistication and more about product design, user experience, and category creation in wellness neurotech.

name: Myndlift
description: Developing a personalized neurofeedback platform that uses EEG data to support mental health and cognitive training at home.
analyst_note: Myndlift sits in the at-home neurofeedback segment, combining EEG-derived training with software delivery for personalized mental-wellness support. It is better understood as a scalable consumer-therapy platform than a deeply differentiated neurotech hardware company.

name: MYndspan
description: Providing consumer-accessible magnetoencephalography (MEG) brain scans to measure brain function and detect subtle signs of cognitive decline earlier.
analyst_note: MYndspan is unusual in bringing MEG, a traditionally expensive institutional modality, into a consumer-facing brain-health offering. This is strategically distinctive but commercially narrow, given the infrastructure and pricing constraints inherent to MEG-based services.

name: Nalu Medical
description: Developing an implantable neuromodulation system with a miniaturized, battery-free architecture for chronic pain and neurological conditions.
analyst_note: Nalu Medical is one of the more commercially advanced miniaturized neuromodulation companies, using a battery-free implant architecture to reduce implant burden in chronic pain treatment. Its FDA-cleared status and acquisition support make it a credible procedural innovator in peripheral neuromodulation.

name: NAOX Technologies
description: Developing an in-ear EEG system for continuous brain activity monitoring in clinical and home settings.
analyst_note: NAOX Technologies is positioned around in-ear EEG as a continuous monitoring modality that could bridge clinical and home use. Its discreet form factor is compelling, though it must still prove that ear-EEG delivers sufficient signal quality for meaningful medical applications.

name: Naqi Logix
description: Developing non-invasive neural earbuds that translate brain, muscle, and facial signals into hands-free digital device control.
analyst_note: Naqi Logix sits at the intersection of consumer BCI, assistive technology, and spatial-computing input. Its positioning is differentiated by using earbuds as a neural-interface form factor, giving it a more familiar hardware pathway than headset-based or implantable control systems.

name: NaviFUS
description: Developing neuronavigation-guided focused ultrasound systems for blood-brain barrier opening and neuromodulation in brain tumors and epilepsy.
analyst_note: NaviFUS sits in the focused ultrasound drug-delivery infrastructure layer, with BBB opening as the clearest clinical and strategic focus. Its profile is unusually advanced for the category, with multiple clinical programs, public-market access in Taiwan, and partnerships around microbubble-enabled CNS delivery.

name: Nervonik
description: Developing a non-invasive peripheral nerve stimulation platform for chronic pain, neurological rehabilitation, and autonomic modulation.
analyst_note: Nervonik is an early-stage non-invasive peripheral nerve stimulation company targeting chronic pain without implants. The segment is highly competitive with established players, and differentiation requires demonstrating meaningful outcome improvements over conventional TENS or more established wearable nerve stimulators.

name: Netholabs
description: Developing large-scale neural-behavioral datasets and whole-brain functional recording systems for ethology and whole-brain emulation research.
analyst_note: Netholabs is best understood as a data infrastructure company for large-scale neural-behavioral datasets and whole-brain functional recording, serving frontier neuroscience rather than clinical markets. Its strategic value would come from owning unique data assets and tooling.

name: Neubond
description: Developing wearable closed-loop neurorehabilitation devices that detect movement intention and stimulate muscles for home-based stroke recovery.
analyst_note: Neubond sits in home-based stroke neurorehabilitation, using wearable sensing and stimulation to make movement-intention training more continuous outside the clinic. Its positioning is differentiated by an Imperial-origin closed-loop interface, with clinical and regulatory translation still early.

name: NeuCyber NeuroTech
description: Developing semi-invasive brain-computer interface implants to decode neural signals for assistive control in patients with paralysis.
analyst_note: NeuCyber NeuroTech sits in China’s state-backed implantable BCI ecosystem, with Beinao-1 focused on assistive control for patients with severe motor impairment. Its positioning is notable for using a semi-invasive cortical-surface approach as part of a broader national push toward domestic BCI development.

name: Neunos
description: Developing an implantable, closed-loop seizure suppression system that detects epileptic activity and delivers transcranial electrical stimulation to terminate episodes.
analyst_note: Neunos is developing a closed-loop seizure suppression platform, pairing detection with responsive stimulation to terminate epileptic activity. This places it in the same high-value therapeutic category as responsive neurostimulation systems, though at a much earlier stage.

name: Neupulse
description: Developing a wearable neuromodulation device using median nerve stimulation to reduce tic frequency in Tourette Syndrome.
analyst_note: Neupulse targets Tourette syndrome through wearable median nerve stimulation, addressing an under-served neurological indication with a non-invasive approach. Its differentiation is largely indication-specific, which can be strategically powerful if clinical efficacy is proven.

name: Neurable
description: Developing BCI-enabled headphones and AI-driven platforms that turn brain signals into control and cognitive insight via everyday wearables.
analyst_note: Neurable is one of the more visible attempts to embed BCI into everyday consumer hardware, shifting EEG from headsets to headphone-like wearables. Its strategic bet is that convenience and design will unlock adoption where traditional BCI form factors have failed.

name: Neuracle
description: Developing an implantable BCI system that decodes motor intent to support hand grasp restoration after cervical spinal cord injury.
analyst_note: Neuracle sits in China’s clinical BCI segment, with NEO positioned around hand grasp restoration after cervical spinal cord injury. Its positioning is differentiated by a minimally invasive extradural interface and a narrow approved motor-restoration use case.

name: Neural Galaxy
description: Developing a precision non-invasive neuromodulation platform that uses individualized brain functional mapping to guide targeted iTBS stimulation.
analyst_note: Neural Galaxy sits in precision non-invasive neuromodulation, using individualized functional brain mapping to guide targeted stimulation across neurological and psychiatric indications. Its positioning is notable within China’s brain-tech ecosystem because it links mapping, decoding, and TMS-based intervention into a multi-indication clinical platform.

name: NeuraLight
description: Extracting eye-movement biomarkers via AI and computer vision from standard webcams or smartphones to accelerate CNS drug development and neurology diagnostics.
analyst_note: NeuraLight is best understood as a pharma-enabling biomarker company, using eye-movement analysis from ordinary cameras to generate objective CNS endpoints for trials and diagnostics. Its modality is low-friction and scalable, giving it strong appeal in decentralized and data-rich clinical settings.

name: Neuralink
description: Developing high-channel-count implantable brain-computer interfaces to restore motor function, enable communication, and eventually merge humans with AI.
analyst_note: Neuralink is the most visible high-bandwidth invasive BCI company, differentiated by its vertically integrated approach spanning surgical robotics, custom chips, and implantable threads. Its profile and capital access are unmatched, though its long-term ambitions still far exceed its current clinical scope.

name: NeuralPulse
description: Creating implantable adaptive neuromodulation that probes brain responses, predicts seizures, and delivers responsive stimulation to prevent them.
analyst_note: NeuralPulse is positioned in adaptive epilepsy neuromodulation, combining brain-response probing with predictive stimulation in a closed-loop implant architecture. It remains highly early-stage but fits squarely within the broader transition from open-loop to responsive therapies.

name: NeuraMatrix
description: Developing neural-interface hardware, chips, and software platforms for invasive BCI research, clinical development, and neural data infrastructure.
analyst_note: NeuraMatrix sits in China’s BCI infrastructure layer, providing chips, neural-interface hardware, software, and data systems for downstream research and clinical translation. Its positioning is notable because it supplies enabling components across invasive, non-invasive, recording, and stimulation workflows.

name: Neuraura
description: Developing wearable bioelectronic devices combining micro-electrodes and stimulation to relieve PCOS symptoms and enhance personalized chronic care.
analyst_note: Neuraura occupies a niche at the intersection of women’s health and bioelectronic medicine, using wearable neuromodulation for PCOS symptom management. Its differentiation comes more from indication choice than modality novelty, giving it a distinct but narrow market position.

name: NeuraWorx
description: Developing bioelectronic neuromodulation technologies to enhance cerebral waste clearance by modulating cerebrovascular dynamics and glymphatic system function.
analyst_note: NeuraWorx is developing neuromodulation technologies aimed at influencing glymphatic and cerebrovascular dynamics, a mechanistically unusual angle compared with mainstream stimulation companies. This makes it scientifically differentiated, though also comparatively speculative.

name: Neurinnov
description: Developing an implantable neurostimulation system that selectively activates nerves to restore hand and arm movement in paralysis.
analyst_note: Neurinnov is building implantable stimulation systems for upper-limb restoration in paralysis, targeting functional recovery rather than general neuromodulation. It sits in the rehabilitation neuroprosthetics category, where clinical proof of meaningful motor gains will be decisive.

name: Neuro Event Labs
description: Providing an AI-powered video and audio seizure monitoring system for epilepsy diagnostics and clinical workflow support.
analyst_note: Neuro Event Labs sits in the clinical seizure-monitoring infrastructure segment, using AI analysis of video and audio to support epilepsy diagnostics and follow-up. Its positioning is differentiated by focusing on objective seizure-event capture within clinical workflows, especially where continuous specialist observation is difficult to scale.

name: Neuro42
description: Building FDA-cleared portable, robotic and AI-driven MRI platforms that bring real-time neuroimaging and interventional guidance directly to patients.
analyst_note: neuro42 is differentiated by combining portable MRI with robotics and AI, targeting bedside imaging and interventional guidance rather than conventional radiology throughput. Its ambition is significant, though execution requires mastering both hardware complexity and hospital integration.

name: Neuroacoustics
description: Using non-invasive acoustic stimulation during sleep to modulate brain oscillations and improve cognition, neurological health, and sleep quality.
analyst_note: Neuroacoustics sits in the sleep and cognition modulation segment, using acoustic stimulation to shape brain oscillations non-invasively. Its approach is low-risk and accessible, though it competes in a crowded field of sleep-focused neurostimulation and wellness products.

name: NeuroBell
description: Providing pocket‑sized, AI‑powered wireless EEG monitoring that detects neonatal seizures at the NICU bedside for early intervention.
analyst_note: NeuroBell targets a clear clinical pain point in neonatal seizure detection, using compact wireless EEG and AI for bedside monitoring in NICUs. Its niche is narrower than adult EEG platforms but potentially more defensible due to workflow specificity and urgency.

name: NeuroBionics
description: Developing minimally invasive implantable bioelectronic fiber systems for targeted neuromodulation therapies and integrated neural interfacing in clinical and research contexts.
analyst_note: NeuroBionics is positioned at the materials-and-interface frontier, developing implantable bioelectronic fibers for targeted neuromodulation and sensing. This places it as enabling infrastructure for future implants rather than a fully formed therapeutic company today.

name: NeuroBrave
description: Developing a hardware-agnostic AI software platform that converts wearable biosensor data into real-time cognitive and emotional state insights.
analyst_note: NeuroBrave is best understood as a software analytics layer for wearable biosensors, translating multimodal data into cognitive and emotional insights. Its differentiation depends on model quality and developer adoption rather than proprietary hardware.

name: Neurocast
description: Passively monitoring brain health via AI-based keystroke and smartphone behavior analysis, delivering real-world neurological data non-invasively.
analyst_note: Neurocast occupies the passive digital biomarker segment, inferring neurological state from keystrokes and smartphone behavior rather than dedicated sensors. This low-friction model is appealing for scale, though it can struggle with signal specificity and clinical credibility.

name: neuroClues
description: Developing an AI-powered eye-tracking biomarker platform to support neurological assessment and monitoring in clinical practice.
analyst_note: neuroClues sits in the clinical neurodiagnostics infrastructure segment, using eye-tracking biomarkers to support neurological assessment and monitoring. Its positioning is differentiated by translating oculomotor measurement into a CE-marked clinician-facing tool for Parkinsonian and broader neurological disorders.

name: NeuroCONCISE
description: Developing wearable EEG-based BCIs that use AI to translate brain activity into control signals for assistive communication and assessment.
analyst_note: NeuroCONCISE develops wearable EEG BCIs for communication and assessment, placing it in the non-invasive assistive interface market. Its challenge is differentiation in a segment crowded with hardware-plus-software EEG entrants.

name: Neurode
description: Offerign a wearable, drug-free headband that stimulates and tracks brain activity for managing ADHD symptoms in just 20 minutes daily.
analyst_note: Neurode is positioned as a consumer-friendly ADHD neuromodulation platform, combining stimulation and tracking in a short daily routine. It straddles wellness and therapy, with the main strategic question being whether it can achieve medical-grade outcomes with consumer-grade simplicity.

name: Neuroelectrics
description: Providing Starstim and Enobio devices for wireless EEG monitoring and non-invasive brain stimulation, applied in research, clinical trials, and therapy.
analyst_note: Neurode is positioned as a consumer-friendly ADHD neuromodulation platform, combining stimulation and tracking in a short daily routine. It straddles wellness and therapy, with the main strategic question being whether it can achieve medical-grade outcomes with consumer-grade simplicity.

name: NeuroEM Therapeutics
description: Developing wearable head devices delivering transcranial electromagnetic treatment (TEMT) for Alzheimer’s and related dementias.
analyst_note: NeuroEM Therapeutics operates in the electromagnetic treatment segment for Alzheimer’s, using wearable TEMT devices aimed at slowing or improving cognitive decline. It sits in a mechanistically distinct but still investigational subset of dementia neuromodulation.

name: Neurolief
description: Delivers wearable, at-home neuromodulation via Relivion, stimulating multiple cranial nerve branches to relieve migraine and depression.
analyst_note: Neurolief is differentiated by its multi-branch cranial nerve stimulation headset, positioning Relivion as a more distributed neuromodulation approach than single-nerve wearables. Its approval pathway and at-home use case give it stronger commercial grounding than many consumer-adjacent stimulation products.

name: NeuroLife
description: Developing wearable neuromuscular sensing and stimulation sleeves for signal-driven hand and arm rehabilitation after stroke and spinal cord injury.
analyst_note: NeuroLife sits in wearable neurorehabilitation, translating Battelle’s neural-bypass work into a non-invasive sleeve for upper-limb recovery. Its launch profile is early commercial translation, with seed funding, licensed platform technology, and FDA clearance still ahead.

name: NeuroLight
description: Developing non-invasive neuromodulation technology using light and sound to induce and replicate targeted brain states.
analyst_note: NeuroLight sits in the brain-state induction segment, using light and sound stimulation to drive targeted cognitive or sleep-related states. It remains closer to wellness and experimental self-regulation than to regulated neuromodulation therapy.

name: Neuromod
description: Developing non‑invasive bimodal neuromodulation device (Lenire) combining tongue and audio stimulation to reduce tinnitus symptoms.
analyst_note: Neuromod has built one of the most distinctive products in tinnitus neurotechnology, using bimodal stimulation of the tongue and auditory system through Lenire. Its FDA clearance and focused indication make it one of the more successful examples of a category-defining neuromodulation company.

name: Neuronic
description: Producing wearable, non-invasive near-infrared light helmets that enhance memory, focus, sleep, and cognitive wellness through photobiomodulation.
analyst_note: Neuronic operates in consumer photobiomodulation, selling wearable light-based devices aimed at memory, sleep, and cognitive wellness. Its differentiation is primarily around at-home usability and branding rather than exclusive underlying science.

name: Neuronoff
description: Developing a minimally invasive, needle-delivered neuromodulation electrode platform to expand access to peripheral nerve stimulation for chronic pain treatment.
analyst_note: Neuronoff is developing a minimally invasive peripheral nerve stimulation electrode platform, aiming to simplify implantation and expand access for chronic pain treatment. Its appeal lies in procedural innovation more than in a new therapeutic mechanism.

name: Neuronostics
description: Applying AI and mathematical modeling to EEG data to generate rapid, digital biomarkers that pinpoint seizure risk and support epilepsy diagnosis.
analyst_note: Neuronostics is a software biomarker company for epilepsy, using EEG and mathematical modeling to quantify seizure risk and diagnostic likelihood. It is differentiated by its modeling depth, though ultimate adoption depends on whether outputs improve decision-making beyond expert interpretation.

name: NeuroOne
description: Developing thin-film implantable electrodes to enable high-precision neural recording, stimulation, and ablation in neurosurgical and neurological care.
analyst_note: NeuroOne sits at the intersection of implantable electrodes and therapeutic intervention, with thin-film systems supporting recording, stimulation, and ablation in epilepsy care. Its FDA-cleared footprint gives it a practical edge over earlier-stage implant component companies.

name: NeuroPace
description: Developing an implantable closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system that detects abnormal brain activity and delivers targeted stimulation to reduce seizures in drug-resistant focal epilepsy.
analyst_note: NeuroPace is one of the few commercially validated closed-loop neuromodulation platforms, demonstrating real-world efficacy in epilepsy. It represents a benchmark for next-generation adaptive neurostimulation systems targeting neurological disorders.

name: Neuropacs
description: Providing AI software that analyzes diffusion MRI scans to differentiate Parkinson's disease from atypical parkinsonian syndromes.
analyst_note: Neuropacs cleared a new FDA De Novo category rather than fitting into an existing one, becoming the first authorized "Parkinsonian syndrome diagnostic aid" and giving it a regulatory moat competitors would need their own submission to match. Its imaging biomarker is now being positioned alongside molecular tests like CSF alpha-synuclein assays, suggesting a combined-biomarker diagnostic pathway rather than a single-test replacement for existing workups.

name: Neurophet
description: Developing AI-driven neuroimaging software to analyze brain MRI scans for early detection and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases.
analyst_note: Neurophet is one of the more mature AI neuroimaging companies in Asia, applying MRI analysis to neurodegenerative disease detection and monitoring. Its public status and regulatory clearances give it greater commercial credibility than many newer imaging software entrants.

name: Neuros Medical
description: Developing an implantable neuromodulation system to treat chronic pain by blocking pain signals in peripheral nerves.
analyst_note: Neuros Medical is differentiated by its use of high-frequency electrical nerve block for chronic pain, targeting signal suppression rather than conventional stimulatory modulation. This mechanistic distinction gives it a clearer identity within the broader pain neuromodulation market.

name: NeuroSigma
description: Developing non-invasive trigeminal nerve stimulation devices to treat pediatric ADHD and other neurological conditions.
analyst_note: NeuroSigma occupies a valuable niche in pediatric neuromodulation, with trigeminal nerve stimulation for ADHD offering a non-drug option in a population sensitive to medication concerns. Its FDA-cleared position is a meaningful barrier in an otherwise lightly populated segment.

name: Neurosity
description: Offering a wearable EEG headset (the Crown) with AI-powered feedback that plays music to enhance focus, mindfulness, and mental state tracking.
analyst_note: Neurosity is positioned as a polished consumer EEG company focused on focus, mindfulness, and productivity, using AI feedback in a lifestyle-oriented device. Its differentiation lies in product experience and community more than in uniquely proprietary sensing.

name: Neurosoft Bioelectronics
description: Developing ultra-soft, foldable neural implants and AI-driven decoding to monitor and modulate brain activity for epilepsy, tinnitus, and rehab.
analyst_note: Neurosoft Bioelectronics is developing ultra-soft implants intended to reduce tissue damage and improve long-term signal quality in epilepsy and related applications. It sits in the same next-generation implant materials trend as Axoft and INBRAIN, though at an earlier stage of translation.

name: Neurosteer
description: Equipping clinicians with a wearable, medical-grade EEG system that delivers real-time neural biomarkers via a head-adhered sensor and cloud analytics.
analyst_note: Neurosteer is differentiated by a compact, single-channel-style EEG form factor paired with cloud analytics, aiming to make neural biomarkers more deployable in routine care. Its practical simplicity is a major advantage, though it may trade off some richness of signal versus full-cap systems.

name: Neurotrack
description: Providing digital cognitive assessments that use eye-tracking and AI to deliver fast, validated screening for dementia and Alzheimer’s risk.
analyst_note: Neurotrack is one of the better-known digital cognitive assessment companies, historically emphasizing eye-tracking and AI for dementia screening. Its FDA-cleared status strengthens its clinical position, though competition in digital cognition has become increasingly crowded.

name: Neurovalens
description: Developing FDA-cleared, non-invasive vestibular neurostimulation wearables (Modius Sleep, Modius Stress) to treat insomnia, anxiety, and metabolic disorders.
analyst_note: Neurovalens is positioned around non-invasive vestibular neurostimulation, an unusual modality that gives it a distinct identity across sleep, anxiety, and metabolic applications. Its FDA-cleared products provide tangible commercial validation, even if the mechanism remains less familiar than mainstream nerve stimulation.

name: Neuroventis
description: Empowering epilepsy and migraine patients with mobile apps (Helpilepsy, MigraineManager) for logging symptoms and safely sharing data with their neurologists.
analyst_note: Neuroventis is best understood as a patient-management and monitoring software company for migraine and epilepsy rather than a core neurotechnology innovator. Its value lies in symptom tracking and data sharing, not proprietary sensing or intervention.

name: Neurowyzr
description: Developing a digital cognitive training platform that uses neuroscience-informed tasks to support mental performance and brain health.
analyst_note: Neurowyzr occupies the digital cognitive training segment, using neuroscience-framed tasks to support performance and brain health. It sits closer to structured brain-fitness software than to regulated neurodiagnostics or therapeutics.

name: NeuroX
description: Developing wearable in-ear EEG devices combined with AI for continuous brain monitoring and early cognitive decline detection.
analyst_note: NeuroX is positioned in the emerging in-ear EEG wellness category, using wearable monitoring for cognitive decline and brain-health insights. Its consumer-first framing makes adoption easier, but also lowers its clinical defensibility.

name: NeuroXess
description: Developing implantable brain-computer interface systems to restore communication and motor function in patients with severe neurological impairment.
analyst_note: NeuroXess is an implantable BCI company focused on restoring communication and motor function, positioning itself in the same broad assistive category as Synchron and Precision Neuroscience. It appears to be at an earlier stage with less public visibility, making differentiation harder to assess.#

name: Neuspera
description: Developing a wirelessly powered implantable neuromodulation system for treating pelvic health and chronic neurological conditions.
analyst_note: Neuspera is one of the more commercially advanced wireless implant companies, using a battery-free architecture for neuromodulation in pelvic and chronic conditions. Its PMA-level status puts it ahead of many similarly miniaturized implant startups.

name: Neuvana
description: Offering Xen, a wearable headphone system that delivers gentle transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation to reduce stress, improve sleep, and boost focus.
analyst_note: Neuvana sits in the consumer vagus nerve stimulation market, embedding tVNS into a headphone-style device aimed at stress, sleep, and focus. It is differentiated more by form factor and lifestyle positioning than by clinical rigor.

name: Neuvotion
description: Providing an AI-guided brain-body interface platform combining minimally invasive BCI and neurostimulation to restore movement after stroke and spinal cord injury.
analyst_note: An already-cleared, non-invasive stimulation product funds the runway toward a minimally invasive BCI still in development, giving Neuvotion commercial revenue that most BCI-stage companies lack. The double neural bypass approach targets movement and sensation together, aligning it with SCI-focused neuromodulation players like Onward Medical.

name: Newronika
description: Developing AlphaDBS, a closed-loop deep brain stimulation implant that adapts therapy in real-time based on brain signals to treat Parkinson’s disease.
analyst_note: Newronika is among the leading closed-loop DBS startups, using adaptive stimulation based on recorded neural signals for Parkinson’s disease. Its CE-marked status and focused indication make it one of the more concrete challengers to incumbent DBS manufacturers.

name: Nexalin
description: Developing non-invasive transcranial electrical stimulation devices for anxiety, insomnia, depression, and broader brain health indications.
analyst_note: Nexalin sits within non-invasive electrical neuromodulation, with a public-company structure and a product line spanning legacy CES and newer higher-current headset systems. Its current positioning is clinically oriented, although the next-generation platform remains tied to additional regulatory and clinical translation in the US.

name: Nexstim
description: Developing navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation systems for non-invasive brain mapping and neuromodulation in clinical and research settings.
analyst_note: Nexstim is a long-standing navigated TMS company, differentiated by image-guided targeting that improves stimulation precision for mapping and therapy. Its public-market presence and procedural maturity place it closer to incumbent neurostimulation infrastructure than startup experimentation.

name: NextMind (Snap AR)
description: Developing non-invasive brain–computer interface software that enables hands-free control of digital interfaces using neural signals.
analyst_note: NextMind helped define the non-invasive AR/VR BCI category by enabling hands-free control through neural signals without implants. Its acquisition by Snap validated the strategic importance of neuro-input layers for spatial computing.

name: NextSense
description: Ear-EEG smartbuds and data platform for continuous brain monitoring focused on sleep, epilepsy and cognitive health.
analyst_note: NextSense is positioned around ear-EEG “smartbuds,” translating continuous brain monitoring into a familiar consumer hardware format. Its strongest differentiation is wearability and passive use, particularly for sleep-related applications.

name: Nia Therapeutics
description: Delivering personalized closed‑loop deep brain stimulation via implantable neuromodulation to counter memory loss in TBI and cognitive disorders.
analyst_note: Nia Therapeutics is developing closed-loop implantable systems for memory restoration in TBI and related disorders, making it one of the few implant companies centered on cognition rather than communication or motor function. That focus is scientifically compelling but clinically demanding.

name: Nimbus
description: Developing cloud-native infrastructure and APIs that enable brain-computer interface developers to collect, train, and deploy neural data applications securely and at scale.
analyst_note: Nimbus is best understood as developer infrastructure for the BCI ecosystem, providing APIs and cloud tooling rather than sensors or therapies. This software-layer role is strategically important if the market expands, though it is still highly contingent on broader category growth.

name: Noctrix Health
description: Developing non-invasive neuromodulation therapies to treat chronic neurological and sleep-related conditions using targeted peripheral nerve stimulation.
analyst_note: Noctrix Health is one of the clearer clinical winners in wearable neuromodulation for sleep-related disorders, using targeted peripheral nerve stimulation in a non-invasive format. Its FDA-cleared status and narrow indication create a focused, defensible market position.

name: Noxisense
description: Developing a portable EEG and radiofrequency stimulation platform to quantify nociceptive function and support diabetic neuropathy assessment.
analyst_note: Noxisense sits in objective neurophysiological pain assessment, combining peripheral small-fiber activation with cortical evoked-response measurement. The platform is early, with strongest evidence around licensed academic IP and prototype-stage clinical translation toward diabetic neuropathy.

name: Nubrain
description: Building foundation models for brain data that decode thoughts into text, images, and speech from non-invasive neural recordings including EEG and fMRI.
analyst_note: Nubrain sits in the brain foundation model space alongside Karavela AI and Alljoined, differentiating through multi-modal decoding ambitions spanning EEG and fMRI rather than a single imaging modality. Its advisory board breadth from tech and neuroscience is notable for an early-stage company, though the company lacks public detail on proprietary datasets or model architecture that would clarify its competitive position versus more established foundation-model efforts.

name: Nudge
description: Developing Nudge Zero, a wearable focused ultrasound headset for non-invasive brain-computer interfacing targeting everyday consumer use.
analyst_note: Nudge is one of the most high-profile consumer ultrasound BCI entrants, benefiting from Fred Ehrsam's profile and the narrative momentum of focused ultrasound as a next-generation non-invasive modality. Its consumer-first positioning distinguishes it from clinical ultrasound neuromodulation companies, though the regulatory and safety validation requirements for consumer ultrasound brain devices remain substantially unaddressed at this early stage.

name: Nuromova Technology
description: Developing AI-powered EEG sports headbands for focus, stress, fatigue, and mental performance tracking during athletic training.
analyst_note: Nuromova Technology sits in consumer neuroperformance, using EEG as a training-layer signal for athletes rather than a clinical assessment workflow. Its current profile appears early and commercially oriented, with public materials focused on pre-orders, CES visibility, and sports-performance positioning.

name: Nuropod
description: Providing a direct-to-consumer auricular vagus nerve stimulation wearable for autonomic regulation, recovery, sleep, and performance support.
analyst_note: Nuropod is best understood as the North American consumer-facing brand for Parasym’s auricular vagal neuromodulation technology. Its positioning sits between wellness neurotech and bioelectronic medicine, with broad autonomic claims and a stronger commercial posture than most early taVNS startups.

name: Nuuron
description: Developing a fully digital Alzheimer’s therapy that uses ultra-high-frequency digital-photonic stimulation via the retina, delivered through VR/AR, to activate memory systems.
analyst_note: Nuuron is developing a fully digital Alzheimer’s therapy using photonic retinal stimulation delivered via VR/AR, making it one of the more unconventional entrants in dementia neuromodulation. Its approach is non-invasive and software-forward, but still very early.

name: Nyxoah
description: Developing an implantable neuromodulation system to treat obstructive sleep apnea by stimulating the hypoglossal nerve.
analyst_note: Nyxoah is an established public neuromodulation company in sleep apnea, using hypoglossal nerve stimulation to compete with other implantable airway therapies. Its scale and maturity place it well beyond startup stage, even if it sits somewhat outside core neurotechnology themes.

name: Oculogica
description: Developing eye-tracking–based neuroassessment software to objectively detect and monitor concussion and traumatic brain injury.
analyst_note: Oculogica is differentiated by using eye-tracking as an objective concussion biomarker, offering a fast and non-invasive alternative to symptom-based assessment. Its FDA-cleared status gives it stronger clinical footing than most digital head-injury tools.

name: Omniscient
description: Developing clinical connectomics software that derives brain network maps from MRI data to support neurosurgical planning and decision-making.
analyst_note: Omniscient occupies the clinical connectomics niche, translating MRI-derived brain network maps into surgical planning support. Its software-only model is attractive for scale, though adoption depends on clinicians trusting connectome outputs in high-stakes decisions.

name: Onward Medical
description: Developing implantable and non-invasive neuromodulation systems to restore movement and autonomic function after spinal cord injury.
analyst_note: Onward Medical is among the most advanced restorative neuromodulation companies, targeting movement and autonomic recovery after spinal cord injury using both implantable and non-invasive systems. Its public status and regulatory progress place it in the upper tier of neurorehabilitation platforms.

name: Open Neurotech
description: Building open-source neurotechnology tools and standards that make advanced brain-computer interfaces accessible to researchers, developers, and creators worldwide.
analyst_note: Open Neurotech sits in the open-source infrastructure layer, aiming to make advanced neurotechnology tools and standards broadly accessible to researchers and developers. Its strategic value is ecosystem enablement rather than proprietary moat creation.

name: OpenBCI
description: Open-source biosensing hardware (EEG/EMG/EKG) and Galea (EEG+biometrics for XR) for BCI research and developer tools.
analyst_note: OpenBCI is one of the most recognized open-source neurotech hardware brands, supplying accessible EEG/EMG systems and Galea for XR-oriented biosensing. Its strength is developer mindshare and community adoption rather than clinical-grade positioning.

name: Openwater
description: Developing wearable, open-source infrared and ultrasound platforms to diagnose and non-invasively treat diseases such as stroke, depression, and tumors.
analyst_note: Openwater is one of the most ambitious companies in non-invasive neurotechnology, aiming to combine diagnostics and treatment through wearable infrared and ultrasound systems. The vision is unusually broad and potentially transformative, though still far ahead of proven clinical execution.

name: Optohive
description: Offering wearable fNIRS brain imaging (HiveOne + AI software) for real-time, high-precision neural monitoring in clinical and research settings.
analyst_note: Optohive is positioned in next-generation wearable fNIRS, pairing hardware with AI software for real-time neural monitoring in research and possible clinical contexts. It remains early and research-oriented, but technically aligned with the trend toward lighter portable hemodynamic sensing.

name: Orbit
description: Developing a wearable brain–computer interface and machine learning models to decode emotional and cognitive states from neural signals.
analyst_note: Orbit is building a wearable BCI and associated machine-learning models for decoding cognitive and emotional states, placing it in the emerging developer-oriented non-invasive neural analytics space. At present it appears more like an enabling platform concept than a differentiated product company.

name: OYMotion Technology
description: Providing EMG, EEG, and bionic prosthetic systems for neural-interface research, rehabilitation, and assistive motor control.
analyst_note: OYMotion Technology sits across neural-interface hardware, bionic prosthetics, and rehabilitation systems, with EMG and EEG sensing linked to assistive motor output. Its positioning is differentiated by a broad hardware portfolio that connects biosignal acquisition, gesture recognition, and prosthetic control.

name: Panaxium
description: Developing an implantable iontronic neurostimulation platform for personalized stroke recovery through brain-surface sensing and stimulation.
analyst_note: Panaxium sits between implantable neuromodulation, bioelectronic medicine, and restorative neurorehabilitation. Its positioning is differentiated by soft iontronic brain-surface interfaces that combine sensing and stimulation for personalized stroke and brain-injury recovery.

name: Panda Surgical
description: Developing a handheld neurosurgical robotics platform with wristed instruments and AI-supported workflow assistance for minimally invasive procedures.
analyst_note: Panda Surgical sits in early neurosurgical robotics infrastructure, with handheld robotic instruments designed for confined cranial and spinal workflows. Its positioning is differentiated by combining wristed micro-instruments with AI-supported workflow assistance in a surgeon-controlled handheld format.

name: Paradromics
description: Developing the Connexus, a fully implantable, high–data-rate BCI that records single-neuron brain signals to restore communication in paralyzed patients.
analyst_note: Paradromics is one of the most serious competitors in the high-bandwidth implantable BCI category, emphasizing single-neuron recording and communication restoration. It is often framed as a peer to Neuralink, though with a more tightly defined initial use case and lower public visibility.

name: PathMaker Neurosystems
description: Developing a non-invasive multi-site direct current stimulation platform for ALS, spasticity, and chronic neuromotor disorders.
analyst_note: PathMaker Neurosystems sits in clinical-stage neuromodulation for neuromotor disorders, with multi-site direct current stimulation aimed at suppressing neuronal hyperexcitability. Its positioning is differentiated by its focus on ALS and spasticity, placing it in a narrower therapeutic segment than most consumer-facing non-invasive stimulation companies.

name: Phantom Neuro
description: Developing minimally invasive muscle implants and AI-driven interfaces enabling intuitive prosthetic and robotic limb control for amputees.
analyst_note: Phantom Neuro takes a peripheral route to prosthetic and robotic control, using minimally invasive muscle implants and AI decoding rather than cortical interfaces. This gives it a pragmatic path to market, with lower procedural burden than brain implants and potentially stronger signal fidelity than surface EMG.

name: Phosphoenix
description: Developing an implantable visual brain prosthesis that electrically stimulates the brain to restore rudimentary vision in blind individuals.
analyst_note: Moving the stimulation target from visual cortex to the LGN directly addresses the narrow visual-field coverage that limited earlier prostheses like Second Sight's Orion. Backing from the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience and EIC grant funding gives the science real institutional weight, though the new probe generation is still pre-clinical.

name: PiEEG
description: Providing open-source EEG and biosignal acquisition hardware for Raspberry Pi-based BCI research, education, and prototyping.
analyst_note: PiEEG sits in the low-cost EEG infrastructure layer, with Raspberry Pi-compatible hardware serving researchers, educators, and BCI prototypers. Its positioning is notable because it treats biosignal acquisition as an open hardware and software stack for experimental neurotechnology development.

name: Piramidal
description: Developing an EEG foundation model to support brainwave interpretation, ICU monitoring, and clinical neurological decision support.
analyst_note: Piramidal sits in the AI neurosoftware layer, with EEG foundation models positioned as clinical infrastructure for brain monitoring and interpretation. Its relevance comes from targeting continuous EEG workflows, where scale, speed, and specialist review capacity are central constraints.

name: Pison Technology
description: Developing a wearable neural sensing platform that uses peripheral nerve signals to enable cognitive monitoring and human–computer interaction.
analyst_note: Pison Technology is building a wearable neural-sensing platform around peripheral nerve and muscle signals, targeting both cognitive monitoring and human–computer interaction. Its strongest strategic angle is that it avoids the friction of head-worn EEG while still offering neural-adjacent signals.

name: PIXYL
description: Applying FDA-cleared, AI-powered analysis to brain MRI scans, enabling rapid lesion detection and volumetric quantification for neurological care.
analyst_note: PIXYL is positioned as an AI neuroimaging workflow company, focused on lesion detection and volumetric MRI analysis across neurological care. Its FDA-cleared status makes it a credible clinical software player, though it competes in an increasingly mature imaging-AI market.

name: PlatoScience
description: Providing clinician-managed tDCS headsets and software for supervised home-based neuromodulation in depression and research settings.
analyst_note: PlatoScience sits in the supervised at-home tDCS segment, with a product stack that combines headset hardware, app control, and clinician dashboards. Its position is relatively mature within non-invasive stimulation because PlatoCare carries EU MDR Class IIa status for depression.

name: Positrigo
description: Developing an ultra-compact dedicated brain PET scanner (NeuroLF®) for accessible imaging of Alzheimer’s and other neurological conditions.
analyst_note: Positrigo occupies a distinctive niche with its ultra-compact dedicated brain PET scanner, offering more accessible neuro-PET imaging than full-body systems. This could expand use in dementia and related disorders, though hardware adoption cycles remain long and capital-intensive.

name: Precision Neuroscience
description: Developing the Layer 7 Cortical Interface, a minimally invasive, high-resolution brain–computer implant to restore communication and independence via thought.
analyst_note: Precision Neuroscience is differentiated by its thin, minimally invasive Layer 7 cortical implant designed to achieve high-resolution recording with less tissue disruption than penetrating arrays. It is one of the more credible near-term implantable BCI companies, positioned between invasive bandwidth and surgical practicality.

name: Precisis
description: Developing a minimally invasive neuromodulation system to treat drug-resistant focal epilepsy through targeted brain stimulation.
analyst_note: Precisis is developing a minimally invasive epilepsy neuromodulation system, positioning itself as a more targeted alternative to broader neurostimulation approaches. Its CE-marked status gives it a stronger clinical foothold than many epilepsy-device startups.

name: Presidio Medical
description: Developing a closed-loop spinal cord stimulation system designed to deliver adaptive neuromodulation for chronic pain management.
analyst_note: Presidio Medical is part of the closed-loop spinal cord stimulation wave, aiming to improve chronic pain management through adaptive therapy. This is an attractive commercial market, though one dominated by large incumbents and requiring strong comparative efficacy data.

name: Prima Mente
description: Developing biological foundation models and clinical research platforms to understand, detect, and prevent neurological disease through AI-driven neuroscience.
analyst_note: Prima Mente is best understood as an AI-and-biology infrastructure company for neuroscience, seeking to build foundation-model-style systems around neurological disease understanding and intervention. Its strategic appeal depends heavily on data ownership and the defensibility of its platform rather than a single near-term product.

name: Prophetic
description: Developing a wearable neuromodulation system designed to induce and stabilize lucid dreaming through non-invasive brain stimulation.
analyst_note: Prophetic occupies the speculative consumer neuromodulation space, aiming to induce lucid dreaming through a wearable stimulation device. It is highly differentiated in branding and use case, though far from clinically grounded neurotechnology.

name: PSYONIC
description: Developing the Ability Hand, an advanced multi-articulated bionic prosthetic with integrated fingertip touch sensing and sEMG control.
analyst_note: PSYONIC differentiates in the myoelectric prosthetics space through its sensorized fingertips that provide haptic feedback, addressing a key gap in conventional bionic hands that provide control but no sensation. Medicare coverage at no out-of-pocket cost is a significant commercial advantage, and its robotics supply agreements with Meta and Apptronik reflect strong hardware credibility beyond the medical device market.

name: Pulsetto
description: Offering a consumer wearable transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation device for stress reduction, improved sleep, and anxiety management through neck-based nerve stimulation.
analyst_note: Pulsetto sits in the growing consumer tVNS market targeting stress, sleep, and anxiety through neck-based vagus nerve stimulation. Its neck placement distinguishes it from auricular tVNS devices like Neuvana and Vagustim, though both approaches target the same physiological mechanism and compete for the same consumer audience.

name: Purple Gaze
description: Developing eye-tracking–based assessment software to support early screening and monitoring of neurodevelopmental conditions.
analyst_note: Purple Gaze uses eye-tracking for early screening of neurodevelopmental conditions, placing it in the pediatric digital biomarker segment. It is a low-burden and scalable modality, though currently more research-oriented than clinically established.

name: QMENTA
description: Empowering imaging teams with a cloud-native AI platform that automates MRI data upload, biomarker extraction, and centralized review for clinical trials.
analyst_note: QMENTA is a cloud-native imaging infrastructure company, helping clinical-trial teams centralize MRI upload, biomarker extraction, and review. Its role is best described as workflow and analytics infrastructure for imaging-heavy drug development rather than a standalone neurodiagnostics company.

name: QuantalX Neuroscience
description: Developing the Delphi-MD, a first-in-class TMS-EEG functional neuroimaging system for early detection and differential diagnosis of brain disorders at the point of care.
analyst_note: QuantalX is unusually well-positioned in functional neurodiagnostics, combining TMS and EEG to generate objective brain-network maps against a normative database — a methodology more akin to functional neuroimaging than standard EEG assessment. Its FDA De Novo authorization establishes a new device category, creating a potential regulatory moat, and Breakthrough Device designations for two indications accelerate its clinical credibility relative to comparably sized companies.

name: Quantanosis
description: Developing a portable robotic ultrasound platform for rapid stroke detection and non-invasive histotripsy-based clot disruption.
analyst_note: Quantanosis sits at the intersection of neurovascular intervention, ultrasound therapy, robotics, and AI-guided stroke triage. Its positioning is differentiated by combining diagnostic transcranial Doppler with histotripsy-based clot disruption, while the platform remains before first-in-human clinical validation.

name: QV Bioelectronics
description: Developing GRACE, an implantable electric field therapy (EFT) device for glioblastoma treatment, targeting tumor cells post-resection to slow recurrence and extend survival.
analyst_note: QV Bioelectronics is pursuing a highly differentiated oncology-neurotech strategy with an implantable electric field therapy device for glioblastoma. It sits at the intersection of neurosurgery, oncology, and bioelectronic medicine, with substantial upside if clinical effects translate.

name: QVITI
description: Developing non-invasive neuromodulation systems that combine transcranial electrical stimulation with immersive VR/XR software to support neurorehabilitation workflows.
analyst_note: QVITI combines tES with immersive XR environments for neurorehabilitation, positioning itself as a hybrid neuromodulation-plus-software workflow platform. This can make therapy more engaging, though it also puts the company in a crowded rehabilitation-tech landscape.

name: Reach Neuro
description: Developing implantable spinal cord stimulation systems (Avantis) that restore voluntary upper-limb movement in chronic stroke survivors.
analyst_note: Reach Neuro is developing implantable spinal cord stimulation systems specifically for upper-limb recovery after stroke, placing it in the restorative neurorehabilitation category. Its indication focus is distinctive, though proving durable motor benefit will be essential.

name: Resolve Stroke
description: Developing software-based ultrasound neuroimaging systems to extract advanced brain biomarkers from raw ultrasound data for bedside monitoring.
analyst_note: Resolve Stroke uses software to derive advanced brain biomarkers from raw ultrasound data, targeting bedside monitoring in acute stroke. This is a technically interesting attempt to extract more value from an underused modality, though still early relative to established stroke imaging workflows.

name: RetiSpec
description: Developing retinal imaging and AI software to detect neurodegenerative disease by analyzing biomarkers in the eye.
analyst_note: RetiSpec is positioned around retinal imaging as a window into neurodegeneration, using AI to identify biomarkers associated with Alzheimer’s and related diseases. Its non-invasive and ophthalmology-compatible approach is attractive, though still research-oriented.

name: ReVision Implant
description: Developing an implantable cortical visual prosthesis that converts camera input into patterned stimulation of the visual cortex to restore functional vision.
analyst_note: ReVision Implant is developing a cortical visual prosthesis for vision restoration, placing it in a small but high-impact category of assistive neurotechnology. Its implantable approach offers potentially stronger performance than external aids, but with all the complexity of invasive translation.

name: Rhovica Neuroimaging
description: Developing a bedside neurosurgical navigation system for safer EVD catheter placement in patients with elevated intracranial pressure.
analyst_note: Rhovica Neuroimaging sits in emergency neurosurgical navigation, with SoNav focused on bedside EVD catheter placement for acute intracranial pressure management. Its positioning is notable because it addresses a specific high-pressure workflow where speed, placement accuracy, and access to navigation infrastructure are closely linked.

name: Rune Labs
description: Providing a cloud-based AI platform (StrivePD) that transforms smartphone and wearable neurology data into actionable insights for precision neurology.
analyst_note: Rune Labs is one of the more commercially grounded digital neurology platforms, integrating wearable and smartphone data into actionable insights for movement disorder management. Its FDA-cleared status and partnerships make it a serious clinical-infrastructure company in precision neurology.

name: Ruten Inc
description: Develops invasive brain-machine interface systems for reconstructive therapy, aiming to restore neural control in conditions unresponsive to conventional options.
analyst_note: Ruten is developing invasive BMI systems for reconstructive therapy, targeting severe conditions where conventional options are limited. It remains early and relatively opaque, making it difficult to distinguish from other preclinical invasive BCI companies on public information alone.

name: Sabi
description: Developing a non-invasive EEG cap that aims to translate internal speech and mental commands into computer input.
analyst_note: Sabi sits in the consumer BCI segment, with its core bet centered on high-density non-invasive EEG and imagined-speech decoding as an input layer for everyday computing. Its positioning is differentiated by the ambition to move EEG from passive state monitoring toward active command generation, placing it closer to interface infrastructure than conventional consumer neurofeedback.

name: Saluda Medical
description: Developing the Evoke System, the first FDA-approved closed-loop spinal cord stimulation system using evoked compound action potentials (ECAPs) to automatically adapt therapy in real time.
analyst_note: Saluda Medical is one of the most clinically advanced closed-loop SCS companies, with the only FDA-approved ECAP-controlled spinal cord stimulation system and the most rigorous RCT evidence base in SCS history. Its objective neurophysiological therapy control represents a paradigm shift relative to conventional programmer-adjusted or patient-adjusted SCS, and its commercial rollout will pressure established SCS incumbents to develop competing closed-loop capabilities.

name: Salvia BioElectronics
description: Developing an implantable neuromodulation system to treat chronic migraine by modulating neural pathways involved in pain processing.
analyst_note: Salvia BioElectronics is one of the more visible migraine neuromodulation startups, using implantable systems to modulate headache-related pathways. Its positioning is attractive because migraine is a large market with poor options for many patients, though it remains investigational.

name: Samphire Neuroscience
description: Pioneering a wearable brain-first neurotechnology, Nettle, that provides non-hormonal brain stimulation to reduce menstrual pain, low mood, and brain fog.
analyst_note: Samphire Neuroscience is differentiated by applying non-hormonal brain stimulation to women’s health symptoms such as menstrual pain, low mood, and brain fog. The indication choice is commercially interesting because it opens a relatively under-addressed segment of consumer-adjacent clinical neurotechnology.

name: Sana Health
description: Delivering a wearable audiovisual neuromodulation mask that uses light and sound pulses via HRV feedback to reduce chronic pain, improve sleep, and ease anxiety.
analyst_note: Sana Health sits in the audiovisual neuromodulation segment, combining light and sound with feedback-driven personalization for pain, sleep, and anxiety. It overlaps with wellness-style neuromodulation but appears to be pushing toward stronger clinical use cases.

name: Sanmai
description: Developing a non-invasive tFUS neuromodulation platform for mental health treatment using AI-enabled acoustic targeting software.
analyst_note: Sanmai sits in the focused ultrasound neuromodulation segment, with Lotus positioned around AI-supported acoustic targeting for psychiatric and neurological indications. Its strategic relevance comes from applying tFUS to mental health, where the established non-invasive stimulation landscape is still largely shaped by TMS and electrical stimulation.

name: Science Corp
description: Developing optogenetic visual prostheses that use microLED arrays to restore sight by stimulating retinal neurons with patterned light.
analyst_note: Science Corp is one of the more serious visual prosthesis companies, using optogenetics and microLED arrays to stimulate retinal circuits with high precision. Its technical ambition is substantial, and it sits closer to advanced translational neuroengineering than to conventional medtech.

name: SecondWave Systems
description: Developing a wearable, non-invasive low-intensity focused ultrasound platform targeting the splenic nerve and autonomic neural pathways for treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases.
analyst_note: SecondWave Systems occupies a distinctive position in the bioelectronic medicine space by applying wearable, non-invasive focused ultrasound to anti-inflammatory neural pathways — a modality and delivery method that differs from both implantable VNS devices and conventional transcutaneous neuromodulation. Its government funding base and JLABS membership suggest early institutional validation, though clinical proof of durable anti-inflammatory efficacy will be required before it can challenge pharmacological biologics.

name: Sens.ai
description: Offering an at-home neurofeedback headset combining EEG, transcranial photobiomodulation, and HRV biofeedback for personalized brain training.
analyst_note: Sens.ai combines EEG neurofeedback, photobiomodulation, and HRV in an at-home headset, positioning itself as a premium brain-training platform. Its broad multimodal stack is commercially appealing but risks feeling more wellness-aggregated than mechanistically focused.

name: Sensars
description: Developing an implantable peripheral nerve stimulation system (SENSY) that provides sensory feedback to amputees, allowing them to feel their prosthetic limbs.
analyst_note: Sensars is developing implantable peripheral nerve stimulation systems that restore sensory feedback in amputees, addressing a critical limitation of conventional prosthetics. This sensory-loop focus gives it a strong rehabilitative rationale, though it remains early-stage.

name: Sense Neuro Diagnostics
description: Developing a non-invasive neurodiagnostic system to objectively assess concussion and brain injury using advanced brain signal analysis.
analyst_note: Sense Neuro Diagnostics targets objective concussion and brain-injury assessment through non-invasive signal analysis, sitting in the same broad problem area as BrainScope and Oculogica. Its key challenge is differentiating sufficiently against more established players with stronger regulatory positions.

name: Senseye
description: Developing eye-tracking–based neurodiagnostic software to objectively assess brain function and support early detection of neurological disorders.
analyst_note: Senseye uses eye-tracking-based neurodiagnostics to assess brain function and detect early neurological dysfunction, making it part of the broader ocular biomarker trend. Its software-only model is scalable, though clinical traction depends on integration into existing assessment pathways.

name: Sensome
description: Developing Clotild, a smart guidewire using impedance-based microsensors and AI to characterize vascular tissue and aid intraoperative decision-making in stroke treatment.
analyst_note: Sensome occupies a highly specific and differentiated procedural niche with its sensorized guidewire for stroke intervention, adding tissue characterization to endovascular navigation. This intraoperative intelligence layer could be valuable in thrombectomy workflows if it proves reliable and easy to integrate.

name: SetPoint Medical
description: Developing an implantable vagus nerve stimulation system for rheumatoid arthritis through neuroimmune modulation of inflammatory pathways.
analyst_note: SetPoint Medical sits in one of the more clinically advanced areas of bioelectronic medicine, using implantable VNS to modulate inflammatory pathways in rheumatoid arthritis. Its positioning is notable because it places neuromodulation inside immune-mediated disease, expanding the category beyond conventional neurological applications.

name: Sevaro
description: Delivering virtual neurology services and tele-neurology programs to provide rapid, specialized neurological care to hospitals.
analyst_note: Sevaro is best understood as tele-neurology workflow infrastructure, delivering specialist care access rather than novel sensing or therapeutic technology. It is neuro-enabled healthcare services more than a core neurotech platform

name: Sharper Sense
description: Developing a wearable, non-invasive neck patch that stimulates sensory-enhancing neural circuits to improve hearing, vision, and touch in real-time.
analyst_note: Sharper Sense is developing a wearable sensory-enhancement patch aimed at boosting hearing, vision, and touch via neural stimulation. The broad enhancement narrative is attention-grabbing, but the company remains early and more consumer-speculative than clinically grounded.

name: ShiraTronics
description: Developing a fully implantable peripheral nerve stimulation system for treatment-resistant chronic migraine through continuous targeted head-based neuromodulation.
analyst_note: ShiraTronics sits in the implantable migraine neuromodulation segment, with a fully implanted peripheral nerve stimulation system for treatment-resistant chronic migraine. Its positioning is differentiated by a focused headache indication and a continuous stimulation model designed for patients with high treatment burden.

name: Sinaptica Therapeutics
description: Delivers personalized, closed-loop rTMS-EEG neuromodulation (SinaptiStim) targeting the default mode network to slow Alzheimer's progression with Phase 2 clinical efficacy.
analyst_note: Sinaptica Therapeutics is one of the stronger emerging companies in dementia neuromodulation, using closed-loop rTMS-EEG to target default mode network dysfunction with growing clinical evidence. Its network-guided approach is more sophisticated than fixed-protocol stimulation systems, giving it a credible precision-therapy angle.

name: Somareality
description: Developing eye-tracking–based algorithms to extract neural signals and monitor cognitive processes in real time.
analyst_note: SOMAREALITY uses eye-tracking algorithms to infer cognitive processes in real time, placing it in the machine-learning-based digital biomarker category. It appears closer to research and experimental analytics than a defined clinical product company.

name: Somnee
description: Developing a personalized, non-invasive neuromodulation system to improve sleep quality through targeted brain stimulation.
analyst_note: Somnee sits in the sleep-focused consumer neuromodulation category, offering personalized stimulation intended to improve sleep quality. It differentiates through personalization, though it remains non-medical and competes in a crowded sleep-optimization market.

name: SONA
description: Developing an adaptive taVNS wearable that combines vagus nerve stimulation, biometric sensing, and audio-guided sessions for stress and recovery.
analyst_note: SONA sits in the consumer neuromodulation segment, using taVNS as an active wellness intervention for stress, recovery, sleep, and performance. Its positioning is differentiated by combining ear-based stimulation, biometric feedback, and app-guided sessions in a familiar wearable format.

name: SOND
description: Developing intelligent sleep earbuds that use real-time biometric sensing and adaptive audio to support consumer sleep improvement.
analyst_note: SOND sits in the consumer sleep neurotechnology segment, with an earbud form factor that combines sleep tracking, biometric feedback, and adaptive audio into an active intervention loop. Its positioning is commercially early and consumer-wellness oriented, with the main strategic distinction coming from closed-loop audio delivery through a familiar in-ear device.

name: SonoMind
description: Developing non-invasive focused ultrasound neuromodulation to precisely stimulate deep brain regions for the treatment of drug-resistant depression.
analyst_note: SonoMind is developing non-invasive focused ultrasound neuromodulation for depression, placing it in one of the more technically exciting next-generation stimulation categories. It remains early, but the modality offers a potential depth-and-precision advantage over electrical or magnetic stimulation.

name: SonoNeu
description: Developing sonogenetic therapies that use ultrasound to control engineered ultrasound-responsive cells for peripheral neuropathy and related indications.
analyst_note: SonoNeu sits at the edge of ultrasound neuromodulation and engineered-cell therapeutics, with sonogenetics as its core technical layer. Its current position is preclinical and consortium-led, with ARPA-H backing and translation dependent on both biological delivery and ultrasound-device development.

name: Sooma Medical
description: Providing a portable tDCS-based neuromodulation system for depression and chronic pain, enabling remote clinician management and scalable home treatment.
analyst_note: Sooma Medical is among the more established home-based tDCS companies, offering clinician-managed depression and pain therapy through a portable system. Its CE-marked position and workflow integration give it more substance than purely consumer stimulation brands.

name: Sound Wave Innovation
