description: Developing transcranial low-intensity pulsed ultrasound devices for early Alzheimer’s disease and related microcirculatory disorders in clinical trials.
analyst_note: Sound Wave Innovation sits in the small group of ultrasound neuromodulation companies applying non-invasive stimulation to neurodegenerative disease. Its positioning is differentiated by a Japan-led pivotal Alzheimer’s trial and a PMDA breakthrough designation, with commercialization tied to clinical readout and approval.

name: Spark Biomedical
description: Developing FDA-cleared, wearable, non-invasive auricular neurostimulation (Sparrow Ascent) to provide drug-free relief for opioid withdrawal and other conditions.
analyst_note: Spark Biomedical focuses on auricular neurostimulation for opioid withdrawal and related conditions, targeting a clinically urgent and commercially meaningful use case. Its wearable, drug-free positioning is attractive in a category where speed of adoption can matter.

name: Spinally
description: Developing FuturaLead, the world’s first intrathecal spinal cord stimulation (iSCS) lead, placed directly on the spinal cord surface, enabling superior efficacy and closed-loop neuromodulation via ECAP sensing.
analyst_note: Spinally is differentiated by its intrathecal spinal cord stimulation lead, which sits directly on the cord surface and aims to improve efficacy while enabling ECAP-based closed-loop control. This is a technically bold hardware innovation in a market otherwise dominated by incremental lead improvements.

name: SpineX
description: Delivering non-invasive spinal cord neuromodulation therapies (SCONE™, SCiP™) to treat neurogenic bladder, cerebral palsy, and related neurological impairments.
analyst_note: SpineX is developing non-invasive spinal cord stimulation systems across bladder dysfunction, cerebral palsy, and related impairments, placing it in restorative neurorehabilitation rather than pain-focused SCS. Its pediatric relevance gives it a distinctive clinical positioning.

name: Spiro Medical
description: Developing an implantable pulmonary neuromodulation system for severe asthma, targeting airway neural reflex pathways through bioelectronic intervention.
analyst_note: Spiro Medical sits at the edge of bioelectronic medicine and respiratory care, applying implantable neuromodulation to severe asthma. Its positioning is strategically notable because it extends neural control approaches into pulmonary disease, where device-based therapy remains a more specialized category.

name: SPR Pain Relief
description: Developing the Sprint PNS System, an FDA-cleared temporary implantable peripheral nerve stimulation device for drug-free treatment of chronic and post-surgical pain.
analyst_note: SPR Pain Relief occupies a clinically distinctive niche with its temporary implantable PNS approach, offering a reversible, 60-day stimulation trial that can provide durable pain relief beyond the treatment period. This carryover effect is a significant differentiator that positions Sprint between TENS/wearable neuromodulation and permanent implants, serving patients who want efficacy without lifetime device commitment.

name: StairMed
description: Developing an invasive BCI platform using ultra-flexible electrodes and robotic implantation for motor restoration and neurological disease applications.
analyst_note: StairMed sits in China’s invasive BCI segment, with ultra-flexible electrodes, wireless implants, and robotic implantation forming the core platform logic. Its positioning is differentiated by a vertically integrated approach that links neural interfaces, implantation tools, and clinical translation workflows.

name: Starfish Neuroscience
description: Building miniaturized, wireless, battery-free BCI chips enabling simultaneous stimulation and recording across multiple brain regions for future therapies.
analyst_note: Starfish Neuroscience occupies the implant-chip infrastructure layer, focusing on wireless, battery-free BCI chips for simultaneous sensing and stimulation. It is better viewed as deep component technology than as a finished therapeutic or assistive product company.

name: Stimvia
description: Developing a non-invasive neuromodulation system using peripheral nerve stimulation to modulate supraspinal circuits for overactive bladder and related chronic indications.
analyst_note: Stimvia uses non-invasive peripheral nerve stimulation for bladder-related indications, making it part of the broader autonomic neuromodulation segment. Its CE-marked status helps, though the category remains less prominent than pain or psychiatric neuromodulation.

name: Subsense Inc
description: Developing the first non-surgical, nanoparticle-based bidirectional BCI, enabling precise brain stimulation and recording without surgery.
analyst_note: Subsense is one of the more speculative BCI entrants, proposing a nanoparticle-based, non-surgical bidirectional interface that would bypass conventional implant limitations. If feasible it would be category-defining, but at present it sits firmly in high-risk frontier science.

name: Subtle Medical
description: Providing AI-powered enhancements for MRI and PET scanning, boosting image clarity, reducing scan time, and enabling dose minimization across all scanners.
analyst_note: Subtle Medical is a mature AI imaging enhancement company, improving MRI and PET quality while reducing scan time or dose across existing hardware fleets. Its broad modality coverage makes it more of an imaging-AI infrastructure business than a neuro-only company, though neurology remains a major use case.

name: Surf Therapeutics
description: Developing a non-invasive ultrasound neuromodulation platform designed to engage the body’s anti-inflammatory neural pathways for treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders.
analyst_note: Surf Therapeutics is developing ultrasound-based neuromodulation aimed at anti-inflammatory neural pathways, making it more adjacent to bioelectronic medicine than central neurotechnology. Its ultrasound approach is distinctive, though still early.

name: Sychedelic
description: Developing EEG-enabled headphones delivering personalised, non-invasive neuromodulation and audio-based stimulation for mental health and cognitive enhancement.
analyst_note: Sychedelic sits at the intersection of consumer EEG, neurofeedback, and audio-based neuromodulation, differentiating through its integrated headphone form factor and closed-loop adaptation of auditory stimulation. Its positioning combines elements of wellness-focused brain-computer interfaces with emerging closed-loop neuromodulation approaches, though its clinical efficacy and regulatory pathway remain to be established.

name: Synaptive Medical
description: Developing integrated neuroimaging, surgical planning, and robotic visualization platforms to improve precision and workflow in neurosurgery.
analyst_note: Synaptive Medical operates at the intersection of neuroimaging and surgical robotics, offering an integrated platform that combines imaging, planning, and intraoperative visualization. Its value proposition lies in workflow integration rather than a single breakthrough modality, competing with established surgical navigation and imaging incumbents. While technologically advanced, its commercial success depends on capital equipment sales cycles and hospital adoption dynamics.

name: Synaptrix Labs
description: Developing a non-invasive, AI-powered brain-computer interface (BCI) headset and proprietary neural-decoding platform to enable individuals with paralysis to control wheelchairs.
analyst_note: Synaptrix Labs is building a non-invasive EEG BCI for wheelchair control in paralysis, positioning itself in the assistive mobility interface segment. Its differentiation depends on decoding accuracy and ease of use in real-world settings rather than a novel modality.

name: SynchNeuro
description: Providing a behind-the-ear EEG wearable that non-invasively predicts blood glucose, sleep quality, and metabolic health via brain-signal analysis.
analyst_note: SynchNeuro is taking an unconventional approach by using behind-the-ear EEG to infer metabolic and physiological states such as blood glucose and sleep quality. This is an ambitious cross-domain biomarker thesis, though one that will require unusually strong validation to gain trust.

name: Synchron
description: Developing the Stentrode, an endovascular, minimally invasive BCI implant enabling paralyzed individuals to control digital devices using thought alone.
analyst_note: Synchron is the leading endovascular BCI company, differentiated by the Stentrode’s ability to reach the brain without open-skull surgery. This minimally invasive route gives it one of the clearest practical advantages in the assistive BCI field, even if bandwidth is lower than intracortical systems.

name: Synchroni
description: Building infrastructure for neurotech apps, enabling non-invasive neural data capture, training, and deployment.
analyst_note: Synchroni sits in the infrastructure layer for non-invasive neurotech, providing tooling for app developers working with neural data capture and deployment. It is strategically sensible but highly dependent on growth in the broader ecosystem it serves.

name: Synergia Medical
description: Developing optoelectronic, MRI‑compatible vagus nerve stimulator (NAO.VNS) to safely treat drug‑resistant epilepsy via long‑life, fast‑charge implant.
analyst_note: Synergia Medical is differentiated by its optoelectronic, MRI-compatible VNS system with long-life and fast-charge implant architecture, addressing a clinically familiar but still innovation-friendly market in epilepsy. It sits within the implantable neuromodulation tier rather than next-generation non-invasive entrants.

name: Syntropic
description: Using 60 Hz non-invasive light stimulation via the eyes to trigger microglia-mediated neuroplasticity, offering a fast, drug-free option for depression and brain recovery.
analyst_note: Syntropic is pursuing light-based brain stimulation for depression and recovery, with a mechanistic narrative centered on neuroplasticity and microglial response. This is unusual and scientifically interesting, but still firmly preclinical.

name: Temple
description: Developing a wearable device for continuous cerebral blood flow monitoring, positioned around brain hemodynamics, performance, and broader brain health applications.
analyst_note: Temple is positioned as a consumer brain-hemodynamics wearable, using cerebral blood-flow monitoring for performance and general brain health. Its wellness framing and unusual physiological angle distinguish it from EEG-heavy consumer neurotech.

name: The Biological Computing Co
description: Building an organic computing platform that integrates living human neurons with modern AI architectures to improve model efficiency and discover novel computational algorithms.
analyst_note: The Biological Computing Company is one of the most commercially ambitious wetware companies, targeting the AI infrastructure market rather than clinical applications, with $25M seed funding suggesting strong investor conviction in biological computing as a complement to silicon. Its Algorithm Discovery platform is a differentiating concept, though its 10-to-20-year roadmap candidly reflects how early the underlying biology-AI integration remains.

name: Theranica
description: Offering Nerivio, a wearable, smartphone-controlled neuromodulation arm band that delivers drug-free, FDA-cleared relief and prevention for migraines.
analyst_note: Theranica has built one of the stronger consumer-friendly clinical neuromodulation products with Nerivio, a smartphone-controlled armband for migraine. Its commercial readiness and regulatory status make it a standout in wearable pain neurotechnology.

name: TheraSonic
description: Developing transcranial focused ultrasound systems to transiently open the blood-brain barrier for targeted CNS drug delivery.
analyst_note: TheraSonic is best understood as an enabling platform for CNS therapeutics, using focused ultrasound, robotics, and neuronavigation to address brain drug delivery. Its position sits before clinical validation, with brain metastases as the clearest initial use case and broader neurological applications remaining translational.

name: Theta Neurotech
description: Developing a wearable EEG patch that predicts epileptic seizures 30–60 minutes before onset, aiming to enable preventative intervention and safer independent living.
analyst_note: Theta Neurotech is developing a seizure-prediction EEG patch for consumers, aiming to forecast events 30-60 minutes before onset rather than simply detect them. That predictive consumer angle is highly differentiated, though it carries significant validation and trust requirements.

name: Thymia
description: Developing digital biomarkers from speech, video, and gameplay to assess and monitor depression and related mental health conditions.
analyst_note: Thymia develops digital biomarkers from speech, video, and gameplay for depression assessment, positioning itself in the multimodal mental-health diagnostics space. Its differentiation is the breadth of behavioral inputs rather than reliance on a single biomarker stream.

name: Time Is Brain
description: Developing a portable brain-monitoring device (BraiN20) for rapid stroke diagnosis and real-time monitoring of brain activity in emergency care.
analyst_note: Time Is Brain is developing a portable stroke-monitoring device for emergency settings, targeting rapid diagnosis and continuous monitoring where treatment windows are narrow. Its clinical value proposition is strong, though success depends on proving actionable performance in fast-paced acute care workflows.

name: Tiposi
description: Developing a portable microwave brain imaging system for rapid stroke assessment and non-invasive brain health detection.
analyst_note: Tiposi sits in the portable neuroimaging segment, using microwave imaging as a lower-infrastructure route to acute brain assessment. Its positioning is strategically notable because it targets the gap between symptom onset and access to conventional imaging in stroke workflows.

name: U: The mind company
description: Developing a consumer-oriented, non-invasive brain stimulation device using amplitude-modulated transcranial pulsed random noise stimulation for cognitive enhancement.
analyst_note: U: The Mind Company is best understood as a consumer tPRNS wellness device positioned below regulated therapeutic devices like Flow Neuroscience's FDA-approved tDCS. Its institutional research claims are difficult to independently verify, and the $350 price point and pre-seed stage suggest a direct-to-consumer lifestyle product with long-term clinical ambitions but no near-term regulatory pathway.

name: UNEEG Medical
description: Developing implantable, long-term EEG monitoring systems to enable continuous brain activity recording for epilepsy management.
analyst_note: UNEEG Medical occupies a highly practical niche in implantable long-term EEG monitoring for epilepsy, enabling more continuous and realistic seizure tracking than hospital-based systems. Its CE-marked status gives it a more advanced translational position than most chronic monitoring startups.

name: Universal Brain
description: Developing a rapid EEG-based brain-function measurement platform combining a dry-electrode wearable with ERP software for psychiatric assessment
analyst_note: Universal Brain is positioned within the narrow but increasingly active category of objective psychiatric biomarkers, pairing a low-cost dry-electrode EEG cap with ERP software to target treatment selection rather than diagnosis in isolation. Its commercialization path through TMS and esketamine clinics ties adoption to existing CPT reimbursement codes rather than requiring new payer infrastructure.`

name: Vagustim
description: Offering a wearable non-invasive device and app to auricularly stimulate the vagus nerve, aiming to reduce stress, improve sleep, digestion, and calm.
analyst_note: Vagustim operates in the consumer tVNS segment, offering auricular stimulation for stress, sleep, and calm through a wearable-plus-app model. It is primarily a wellness product, differentiated more by accessibility than clinical rigor.

name: Vielight
description: Developing at-home photobiomodulation headsets and applicators that use near-infrared light to support cognitive enhancement, mood, sleep, and overall brain wellness.
analyst_note: Vielight is one of the more visible photobiomodulation brands in consumer neurotech, selling light-based devices for cognition, mood, and sleep. Its broad claims and home-use format make it commercially accessible, though its scientific positioning remains mixed.

name: ViewMind
description: Enabling non-invasive, VR headset-based assessment of neurocognitive health using eye movement biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity.
analyst_note: ViewMind uses VR-based eye-tracking to assess neurocognitive function, creating a more immersive and standardized testing environment than conventional screen-based tools. It sits in the promising but still emerging VR diagnostics category for dementia and cognitive decline.

name: Vistim Labs
description: Providing AI-powered EEG brain mapping software that enables point-of-care monitoring of dementia, correlating with amyloid, tau, atrophy, and cognitive endpoints.
analyst_note: Vistim Labs is developing EEG-based dementia monitoring software that correlates neural signatures with pathology and cognitive endpoints, giving it a more disease-linked framing than generic brain-mapping tools. It remains early but sits in a clinically important biomarker segment.

name: Vonova
description: Developing Cerebro, a minimally invasive endovascular brain access platform that enables treatment of neurological disorders without drilling through the skull.
analyst_note: Vonova is best understood as neurovascular access infrastructure, developing an endovascular platform that could simplify delivery of therapies to the brain without open craniotomy. Its value lies in enabling other interventions rather than being the intervention itself.

name: VoxNeuro
description: Providing EEG-based cognitive health assessments using event-related potentials to support objective evaluation of brain function across clinical settings.
analyst_note: VoxNeuro sits in the objective cognitive assessment segment, using ERP-derived EEG biomarkers as an adjunct to behavioral neuropsychological testing. Its position is clinically oriented, with regulatory status in Canada and the US and a software-led model built around standard EEG acquisition.

name: Wave Neuroscience
description: Using EEG-driven brain mapping and personalized neuromodulation protocols to optimize neural activity for cognitive and mental-health outcomes.
analyst_note: Wave Neuroscience combines EEG-derived brain mapping with personalized neuromodulation, positioning itself as a precision mental-health platform. Its strength is the closed-loop personalization narrative, though the category has many similar “map then stimulate” propositions.

name: Wearable Devices
description: Developing the Mudra wristband, a neural gesture recognition wearable that decodes hand and finger movement intent from neuromuscular signals for human-computer interaction.
analyst_note: Wearable Devices occupies a niche in non-contact peripheral EMG gesture recognition, with Apple Watch-compatible hardware targeting the consumer AR/VR and gesture control market. Its non-contact sensing differentiator is technically interesting, though the consumer gesture control market remains nascent and dependent on broader AR/VR hardware adoption.

name: Wellumio
description: Developing a portable, battery-powered MRI-based brain imaging device for point-of-care stroke diagnosis in acute care settings.
analyst_note: Portable, contrast-free MRI at the bedside solves a real infrastructure problem in acute stroke care: minutes matter, and fixed scanners aren't always reachable in time. Regulatory and investor momentum (breakthrough-track ambitions, a $9.75M oversubscribed round) suggest the market agrees the timing is right, even with clinical validation still in progress.

name: Winterlight Labs
description: Analyzing natural speech via tablet to extract vocal biomarkers that detect and monitor cognitive impairment, enabling objective, scalable assessments.
analyst_note: Winterlight Labs is a speech biomarker company focused on cognitive impairment, extracting subtle vocal features through tablet-based assessment. As an acquired company, it is best viewed as a validated capability integrated into larger digital cognition platforms.

name: WISE
description: Developing soft, stretchable implantable electrodes that improve safety and performance of neuromodulation leads in neuromonitoring and neurostimulation.
analyst_note: WISE is a component-level neurotechnology company developing soft, stretchable implantable electrodes that improve safety and performance of neural interfaces. Its value lies upstream in enabling better implants, making it a materials-and-manufacturing play rather than a direct therapeutic company.

name: Wisear
description: Developing neural interface technology that enables hands-free control of consumer devices through brain–computer interaction.
analyst_note: Wisear focused on ear-based neural interfaces for hands-free device control, positioning itself in the consumer tech and smart-earbuds segment. Its acquisition suggests strategic value in subtle, wearable neural inputs for mainstream electronics.

name: X-trodes
description: Developing rapid-application dry EEG electrode systems to enable high-quality brain signal acquisition without gels or skin preparation.
analyst_note: X-trodes is differentiated by rapid-application dry electrode systems that remove many of the frictions associated with traditional EEG preparation. This makes it a practical infrastructure company improving usability across sleep, research, and broader biosignal acquisition.

name: XanaStim
description: Developing wearable auricular vagus nerve stimulation systems for primary insomnia, with physiological monitoring and broader clinical neuromodulation applications.
analyst_note: XanaStim sits within the emerging group of auricular VNS companies trying to make peripheral neuromodulation more wearable and dose-tracked. Its current positioning is clinically oriented, with insomnia as the clearest entry point and regulatory translation still unconfirmed.

name: Yneuro
description: Developing neural authentication software that uses unique neural signatures as a biometric for secure digital identity and access.
analyst_note: Yneuro sits in the niche category of neural biometrics, using brain-derived signatures as a form of authentication. It is an interesting application-layer business, though likely narrower in commercial scope than core neurodiagnostics or interface platforms.

name: Zander Labs
description: Developing portable, high-fidelity EEG hardware and passive BCI systems for real-time cognitive monitoring and neuroadaptive applications.
analyst_note: Zander Labs is positioned around passive BCI and cognitive monitoring, combining portable EEG hardware with neuroadaptive software applications. Its emphasis on real-time mental-state adaptation differentiates it from simple signal-acquisition vendors.

name: ZenoWell
description: Providing ear-worn taVNS devices for sleep, stress, recovery, and daily autonomic regulation in consumer wellness.
analyst_note: ZenoWell sits in the consumer auricular VNS segment, with a compact ear-worn form factor and broad wellness claims around sleep, stress, pain, and recovery. Its public positioning is commercially oriented, with limited independent company-specific validation and future sensing ambitions tied to partnerships.

name: Zeta Surgical
description: Developing AI-enabled surgical navigation systems for cranial procedures, neuromodulation targeting, and point-of-care image-guided intervention.
analyst_note: Zeta Surgical sits in the clinical navigation infrastructure layer for neurosurgery and neuromodulation targeting, with AI image analysis and frameless navigation supporting cranial procedural workflows. Its positioning is strategically notable because it links surgical guidance, interventional neurology, and TMS targeting within a cleared medical-device platform.

name: Zhiran Medical
description: Developing an invasive flexible-electrode BCI platform for high-throughput neural recording, motor restoration, and communication-assistive applications.
analyst_note: Zhiran Medical sits in China’s flexible invasive BCI segment, with a platform aimed at high-throughput recording, motor restoration, and communication support. Its positioning is notable for combining flexible electrodes, implantable acquisition hardware, decoding software, and surgical robotics into a clinical-stage system.
